docs.t: 2. What is established Data and AI maturity matrix (levels only, no scores)
docs.x: - Across the 29 company-level A6 entries, 18 sit at concept, prototype or pilot, and none reaches demonstrated outcome [CLM-006054]. - Lilly has the largest evidenced infrastructure build and the only owned-compute and data-as-product pair; the registry shows no scientific, cycle-time or financial result from either [CLM-006053] [CLM-006007]. - J&J's devices carry the only regulator records among the four companies' AI-adjacent products, and those records concern devices, not discovery [CLM-006054] [CLM-014022] [CLM-014025]. - AbbVie internalises data (ARCH, a knowledge graph, not generative AI) and buys models (BigHat, Valkai) [CLM-006032] [CLM-006035] [CLM-000285]. - Takeda's disclosed strategy is partnership-led, and its 2026 integrated report adds company-reported operating items in manufacturing AI and workforce adoption that the earlier baseline did not have [CLM-006053] [CLM-014041] [CLM-014043].

docs.t: 3. Answers to the two comparison questions Data and AI maturity matrix (levels only, no scores)
docs.x: Which technology ecosystem is most defensible? The registry cannot support a ranking. The candidate moat the A6 analysis identifies is Lilly's proprietary experimental data (company-estimated to cost over USD 1bn to generate) paired with a federated platform, but the same analysis rates the moat claim only partially supported and finds no outcome [CLM-006055] [CLM-000280]. Federated consortia and open models are available substitutes [CLM-006056]. The statement "Lilly has the most defensible ecosystem" is therefore a (HYPOTHESIS) , not a finding. Which AI investments are operationally meaningful? Operationally meaningful here means operational or higher status plus a disclosed operating scale. On that test the items are LillyPod (compute online) [CLM-006004], ARCH (internal graph with disclosed size) [CLM-006032], Takeda's Lessines predictive maintenance and plasma nomograms (company-reported scale, benefit unquantified) [CLM-014041] [CLM-005060], and J&J's gen-AI quality-control tool (qualitative) [CLM-006021]. No item has an independently verified effect on cost, cycle time or revenue. Announcement-stage items (NVIDIA lab, Valkai, Isomorphic, OpenAI) are not operationally meaningful on this evidence [CLM-000281] [CLM-000285] [CLM-006012] [CLM-006011].

docs.t: LES-01 Manufacturing capacity as the binding constraint on a blockbuster (LLY) Lessons for Takeda from Lilly, J&J and AbbVie
docs.x: - What they did. Lilly raised capex from USD 1.3bn (FY2021) to USD 7.8bn (FY2025) and announced more than USD 50bn of U.S. commitments after tirzepatide supply fell short; the FDA removed tirzepatide from the shortage list on 2024-10-02. Most announced sites are still pre-operating, with operating evidence only for Concord, Kinsale and the Lebanon genetic-medicine plant. [CLM-000168] [CLM-000172] [CLM-001039] [CLM-001066] [CLM-014017] [CLM-014008] [CLM-014014] - Transferability: partially. Takeda's plasma-derived therapies are capacity-bound (collection centres and fractionation) and it has a USD 230m Los Angeles expansion, so the capacity logic transfers. The lesson to copy is to track operating capacity, not announced capacity. Takeda's FY2025 capex of JPY 426.9bn includes intangible assets and is not comparable with Lilly's property, plant and equipment capex. (INTERPRETATION) - Takeda baseline class. EXISTING STRENGTH (class 2: plasma network and PDT manufacturing). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005063] [CLM-005065] [CLM-005007] - Internal validation needed. IVB-006

docs.t: LES-02 Cash-pay direct-to-patient channel (LLY) Lessons for Takeda from Lilly, J&J and AbbVie
docs.x: - What they did. Lilly launched LillyDirect on 2024-01-04, sold Zepbound self-pay vials from August 2024 and cut prices on 2025-12-01 to USD 299 / 399 / 449. The company says over 1 million patients accessed treatments through it in 2025; the 10-K gives no dollar share, and copay-accumulator and anti-kickback limits restrict combining discounts with insurance. [CLM-001042] [CLM-007002] [CLM-007004] [CLM-007005] [CLM-007010] - Transferability: does not transfer. Cash-pay scaled in an uninsured-gap category (obesity). Takeda's main products are infused or specialty-distributed biologics and plasma therapies sold through payer coverage and hubs, so a cash channel fits poorly. Home and subcutaneous conversion (LES-21) is the better-evidenced mechanism. (INTERPRETATION) - Takeda baseline class. EVIDENCE GAP (class 14: patient services and market access). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005072] [CLM-007037] - Internal validation needed. IVB-013

docs.t: LES-03 Data-for-access platform (federated learning) (LLY) Lessons for Takeda from Lilly, J&J and AbbVie
docs.x: - What they did. Lilly launched TuneLab on 2025-09-09, giving selected biotechs access to Lilly-trained ADMET and safety models in exchange for federated data contributions, with Benchling distribution to more than 1,300 customers opt-in later in 2026. No uptake, retraining count or scientific outcome is disclosed. [CLM-000280] [CLM-006008] [CLM-014055] [CLM-014056] [CLM-006055] - Transferability: partially. Takeda is already in a multi-pharma federated consortium (AISB) and could be a data-for-models participant, which is a cheaper position than building a rival platform. The platform's value is unproven, so participation should wait for independent results. (INTERPRETATION) - Takeda baseline class. EXISTING BUT UNDERDEVELOPED (class 9: enterprise data and AI platform, outcomes unproven). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005058] [CLM-005049] [CLM-006042] - Internal validation needed. IVB-001

docs.x: - What they did. Lilly built a remote robotic laboratory (Life Sciences Studio) and divested it to the CRO Arctoris in 2024; the reason is undisclosed. docs.t: LES-05 Growth concentration, price erosion and payer leverage (LLY) Lessons for Takeda from Lilly, J&J and AbbVie
docs.x: - What they did. Tirzepatide reached 56.0% of Lilly's FY2025 revenue (15.6% in FY2023). Realised prices fell 5% in Q4 2025 and 15% in Q3 2026 while volume rose 46% and 53%; CVS Caremark removed Zepbound from its template formularies for 15 months (1 July 2025 to 1 October 2026); Trulicity and Verzenio face Medicare-set prices from 2028. [CLM-001003] [CLM-014003] [CLM-014004] [CLM-007011] [CLM-007013] [CLM-008015] - Transferability: transfers. Entyvio is 21% of Takeda's revenue, faces Medicare negotiation from 2028 and a coming biosimilar event. Lilly's record shows that volume growth in a dominant franchise comes with net-price pressure and PBM leverage, so Takeda should plan for price erosion in its core franchise, not only for volume loss. (INTERPRETATION) - Takeda baseline class. EXISTING STRENGTH (class 1: GI and immunology franchise). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005009] [CLM-005017] [CLM-008022] - Internal validation needed. docs.x: - What they did. J&J had TREMFYA (IL-23) on the market with Crohn's and UC labels and approved the oral IL-23 peptide ICOTYDE on about 2026-03-17. In FY2025 Tremfya grew USD 1,485m, offsetting about 35% of Stelara's USD 4,283m loss, yet Immunology still fell 11.8%. J&J's record also shows that even a pre-launched successor offsets only part of the loss in the first year. (INTERPRETATION) - Takeda baseline class. docs.x: - What they did. docs.t: LES-14 Contracting defence against PBM-driven biosimilar substitution (ABBV) Lessons for Takeda from Lilly, J&J and AbbVie
docs.x: - What they did. AbbVie kept at least 97% of adalimumab volume through March 2024 with rebate-for-access contracts, then supplied a co-branded Humira to CVS's Cordavis when Caremark removed Humira from template formularies on 2024-04-01; U.S. Humira revenue still fell 41% in 2024 and 57% in 2025. [CLM-003007] [CLM-003008] [CLM-003009] [CLM-003010] [CLM-007016] - Transferability: partially. PBM private labels now handle large biosimilar events (nine Stelara biosimilars by July 2025, four from PBM-affiliated labels), so payer contracting depth matters as much as patents. Takeda has no public evidence on rebate or contracting structure, and two Entyvio biosimilar BLAs are under FDA review. (INTERPRETATION) - Takeda baseline class. docs.x: - What they did. AbbVie recorded a USD 4.5bn impairment in Q4 2024 after emraclidine failed, 54% of the USD 8.3bn Cerevel net price. The first two novel approvals of the replacement set came in August 2026, after the FY2025 close Mostly in-licensed or acquired programmes (Nimbus, Protagonist, Keros, Arrowhead); oveporexton is an in-house discovery per Takeda [CLM-005008] [CLM-005001] [CLM-005011] [CLM-005029] [CLM-005032] [CLM-005050] [CLM-005048] Lilly Tirzepatide launch (Mounjaro 2022, Zepbound 2023) replaced Trulicity and Alimta and then supplied most of group growth Mounjaro + Zepbound USD 36,507m = 56.0%

docs.t: 2. Why the four cases cannot be ranked on one number Loss-of-exclusivity (LOE) resilience: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie, Takeda
docs.x: 1. Different cliff sizes. Humira was 36.6% of AbbVie revenue at peak; Stelara 12.8% of J&J's; Vyvanse 9.9% of Takeda's (FY2023 base) (computed) [CLM-003004] [CLM-002022] [CLM-005015]. A smaller cliff is absorbed more easily regardless of management quality, so equal replacement ratios would not imply equal capability (INTERPRETATION) . 2. Different elapsed time. AbbVie's cliff is observed for three years, J&J's for two, Takeda's for two. A replacement ratio computed at different ages is not a like-for-like measure. The only like-for-like comparison available is year-2 decline: Humira -57.7% (2024 vs 2022 peak), Stelara -44.0% (FY2025 vs FY2023 peak), Vyvanse -52.0% (FY2025 vs FY2023) (computed) [CLM-003002] [CLM-002022] [CLM-005015]. 3. Different segment boundaries and acquisitions. J&J's replacement mixes organic growth with acquired revenue (Intra-Cellular, Abiomed, Shockwave) [CLM-002041] [CLM-002011] [CLM-002027], which the registry does not separate fully; AbbVie's replacement products were pre-existing [CLM-003084]. J&J's "ex-Stelara +12.3%" therefore overstates organic resilience by an amount only partly disclosed (about one point per J&J) [CLM-002075]. 4. Different currencies and fiscal years. Takeda's JPY series embeds exchange-rate effects (FY2025: -1.7% actual versus -2.7% constant) [CLM-005001], and its FY ends in March, so its FY2025 overlaps the other three companies' 2025 by nine months only [CLM-005000]. 5. Different price mechanisms. AbbVie's defence was contracting (at least 97% of adalimumab volume retained through March 2024) followed by a CVS Caremark / Cordavis co-branded arrangement; the steepest declines (-41% in 2024, -57% in 2025 for U.S. Humira) followed the April 2024 formulary change, which the registry treats as association, not proven causation [CLM-003007] [CLM-003008] [CLM-003010]. J&J's Stelara faced nine biosimilars including four sold by PBM-affiliated private labels by July 2025, plus a Medicare negotiated price 66% below the 2023 list price from January 2026 [CLM-007016] [CLM-008008]. Takeda has not yet faced its Entyvio event [CLM-005017]. Comparison status: valid as a side-by-side

docs.t: 1. Why is Lilly winning where it wins? Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline
docs.x: Lilly's revenue rose from USD 28.3bn to USD 65.2bn (FY2021 to FY2025), 23.2% a year (computed) , because tirzepatide went from first revenue in 2022 to 56.0% of sales [CLM-000133] [CLM-000137] [CLM-001001] [CLM-001003]. Pre-tax margin rose from 21.7% to 39.5% and gross margin from 74.2% to 83.0% while R&D roughly doubled [CLM-001007] [CLM-001005] [CLM-000143] [CLM-000147]. The mechanisms evidenced are: a launched incretin with strong trial results (SURMOUNT-1 weight loss up to 20.9%) [CLM-001056]; capacity spending (capex USD 1.3bn to 7.8bn) after a shortage that ended in 2024 [CLM-000172] [CLM-001066]; a cash-pay channel [CLM-001042]; and a follow-on oral and triple-agonist pipeline [CLM-001030] [CLM-001060]. What the evidence does not show is durability: realised prices fell 15% in Q3 2026 and about USD 900m of that quarter was one-off [CLM-014003]. (INTERPRETATION) Lilly is winning in a category where demand exceeded supply; the registry does not show whether the advantage persists once supply and competition normalise.
docs.h: 1. Why is Lilly winning where it wins?

docs.t: 2. What makes J&J's pharma and MedTech combination distinctive, and where is the synergy unevidenced? Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline
docs.x: J&J is the only one of the four with a MedTech segment (USD 33.8bn) beside Innovative Medicine (USD 60.4bn) [CLM-000253]. MedTech earns a 12.2% segment margin against 36.9%, grew 2.5% in Q3 2026, and J&J announced the Orthopaedics separation [CLM-002004] [CLM-002060] [CLM-002037]. J&J claims cardiovascular leadership across Abiomed, Biosense Webster and Shockwave; no cross-segment revenue synergy is disclosed, so the pharma and MedTech synergy is unevidenced [CLM-002074]. The distinctive, evidenced feature is diversification: the largest brand is 15.2% of revenue and Cardiovascular grew 15.8% [CLM-002073] [CLM-002028]. Offsetting evidence: Impella recalls and the Varipulse pause [CLM-002046] [CLM-002044].
docs.h: 2. What makes J&J's pharma and MedTech combination distinctive, and where is the synergy unevidenced?

docs.t: 3. How did AbbVie absorb the Humira loss of exclusivity? Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline
docs.x: Global Humira fell from USD 21,237m (2022) to 4,540m (2025), -78.6% (computed) , after U.S. exclusivity ended on 2023-01-31 [CLM-003002] [CLM-003000]. Skyrizi plus Rinvoq rose USD 18,179m against a Humira loss of 16,697m; total revenue passed its 2022 peak only in 2025 [CLM-003014] [CLM-003015]. Three mechanisms are evidenced: successors already marketed and extended across Humira's indications [CLM-003084] [CLM-003016]; rebate-for-access contracting that held at least 97% of volume to March 2024, then a Cordavis co-brand [CLM-003007] [CLM-003008]; and patent settlements (Rinvoq entry not before April 2037) [CLM-003021]. Steep U.S. declines came after the April 2024 formulary change, which is an association, not proven causation [CLM-003010]. See loe resilience comparison.md.
docs.h: 3. How did AbbVie absorb the Humira loss of exclusivity?

docs.t: 4. Who converts R&D into commercial outcomes best? Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline
docs.x: Metric definitions and results are in rd investment and productivity.md and pipeline and revenue dependence.md. On R&D intensity, Lilly fell from 24.5% to 20.5%, J&J stayed at 15.6-15.7%, AbbVie rose from 12.6% to 14.9%, Takeda stayed at 14.7-15.0% (computed) [CLM-001006] [CLM-000085] [CLM-000015] [CLM-005004]. On the share of FY2025 revenue from molecules approved after 2021-11-21, Lilly is at least 56.0%, J&J at least 3.2%, AbbVie at least 1.8% and Takeda not computable (computed) [CLM-001003] [CLM-002024] [CLM-003036] [CLM-003037]. That comparison is invalid as a productivity ranking : it rewards new-molecule growth and penalises lifecycle growth (Skyrizi and Rinvoq), acquired assets are mixed with in-house ones (sponsor of record for Elahere is ImmunoGen, for Epkinly Genmab) [CLM-012013] [CLM-012014], approval counts (8, 5, 5, 3) are small and include 2026 approvals funded earlier [CLM-012000] [CLM-012007], and R&D accounting boundaries differ [CLM-000270]. The evidence supports only a narrower statement: Lilly's recent growth comes from a molecule approved inside the window, AbbVie's from molecules approved before it (INTERPRETATION) .

docs.t: 5. Who has the most defensible technology ecosystem? Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline
docs.x: The registry cannot support a ranking. Lilly has the largest evidenced build (LillyPod, TuneLab, external model partners) with no outcome shown; J&J has the only regulator records (devices, not discovery); AbbVie has an internal knowledge graph; Takeda is partnership-led with 2026 company-reported operating items [CLM-006004] [CLM-000280] [CLM-014022] [CLM-006032] [CLM-014041]. Of 29 company-level entries, 18 sit at concept, prototype or pilot and none shows a demonstrated outcome [CLM-006054; counts computed from data ai maturity matrix.md — INTERPRETATION]. "Lilly is most defensible" is a (HYPOTHESIS) resting on proprietary data (company-estimated at over USD 1bn) [CLM-006055] [CLM-000280]. See data ai maturity matrix.md.
docs.h: 5. Who has the most defensible technology ecosystem?

docs.t: 6. Which AI investments are operationally meaningful? Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline
docs.x: Operational status plus disclosed scale: LillyPod (1,016 GPUs) [CLM-006004], AbbVie's ARCH (124 TB, over 30 million nodes) [CLM-006032], Takeda's 170+ Lessines predictive-maintenance agents and plasma nomograms [CLM-014041] [CLM-005060], and J&J's quality-control tool (qualitative) [CLM-006021]. None has independent evidence of effect on cost, cycle time or revenue. NVIDIA lab, Valkai, Isomorphic and OpenAI are announcements [CLM-000281] [CLM-000285] [CLM-006012] [CLM-006011].

docs.t: 7. Who has repeatable discovery and development capability? Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline
docs.x: Evidence of repetition, not of quality: Lilly eight novel approvals across incretin, immunology, neurology and oncology [CLM-012000] [CLM-012007]; J&J five spanning bispecifics, a TKI, an FcRn antibody and an oral peptide [CLM-012008] [CLM-012012]; AbbVie five, mostly acquired or partnered, with growth from supplements [CLM-012013] [CLM-012033]; Takeda three, with three Phase 3 readouts delivered positive on the 2024 plan [CLM-012018] [CLM-005042]. Repeatability is partly unproven for all: AbbVie's neuroscience record is one approval and one failure, Takeda's replacement set arrived in August 2026, and Lilly's expensed 2023-2025 purchases had no approval by cutoff [CLM-012148] [CLM-005029] [CLM-009000]. Attrition appears in every company: see strengths and vulnerabilities.md and rd investment and productivity.md.

docs.t: 8. Which partnerships create durable options? Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline
docs.x: Option structures exist at AbbVie (ADARx, Calico, Gubra, Ichnos), Takeda (Innovent licence, equity and option) and Lilly (Beam opt-in, CVRs) [CLM-009061] [CLM-009068] [CLM-009062] [CLM-009060] [CLM-009078] [CLM-014058] [CLM-009099]. No option from the window has yet produced an approved product, so durability is a (HYPOTHESIS) [CLM-009095] [CLM-009097]. Realised value from partnerships so far: J&J Momenta (IMAAVY) and Intra-Cellular (CAPLYTA MDD), Lilly Loxo (Jaypirca), AbbVie ImmunoGen (Elahere), Takeda HUTCHMED (Fruzaqla) and Protagonist (Mimrylo) [CLM-009044] [CLM-009031] [CLM-009015] [CLM-009056] [CLM-012018] [CLM-012020]. Deal-value comparisons are invalid across bases; see partner ecosystem comparison.md.

docs.t: 9. What does each do better than the other two, and where is each vulnerable? Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline
docs.x: See strengths and vulnerabilities.md. In one line each, on evidence: Lilly combines growth with margin expansion and capacity build [CLM-000137] [CLM-001007] [CLM-000172]; J&J absorbs a large LOE with a diversified base [CLM-000253] [CLM-000254]; AbbVie replaces a dominant franchise with pre-built successors [CLM-003014]; Takeda has a plasma-derived franchise and in-house orexin discovery [CLM-005063] [CLM-005048]. Largest vulnerabilities: Lilly, concentration of 56.0% and price erosion [CLM-001003] [CLM-014003]; J&J, talc and a still-falling Stelara [CLM-002062] [CLM-002060]; AbbVie, successor concentration at 42.3% (computed) and a USD 4.5bn neuroscience write-down [CLM-000266] [CLM-003057]; Takeda, Entyvio at 21% with exclusivity loss ahead, flat revenue and the AMITIZA provision [CLM-005009] [CLM-005017] [CLM-005001] [CLM-005014].

docs.t: 10. What would change positions by 2035? (HYPOTHESIS; anchors are evidenced dates) Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline
docs.x: - Lilly: tirzepatide patent to 2036; Trulicity patent 2027; Trulicity and Verzenio negotiated prices from 2028; retatrutide, lepodisiran and orforglipron outcome trials read out 2029-2031 [CLM-000250] [CLM-008015] [CLM-001047] [CLM-001050] [CLM-001045]. - J&J: Stelara erosion through 2026-2027, talc resolution needing 95% participation, the Orthopaedics separation 18-24 months after October 2025, DARZALEX concentration (patent dates not in the registry) [CLM-002060] [CLM-002062] [CLM-002030] [CLM-002073]. - AbbVie: Vraylar patent September 2029 (analyst source), Skyrizi and Rinvoq composition patents 2033, Rinvoq entry 2037, obesity and in-vivo CAR-T programmes at Phase 1 [CLM-003029] [CLM-003021] [CLM-003073] [CLM-003072]. - Takeda: Entyvio exclusivity loss in the latter half of the decade and 2032 patents, Trintellix generics after December 2026, launch execution of oveporexton, rusfertide and zasocitinib, Amitiza appeal [CLM-005017] [CLM-005016] [CLM-005035] [CLM-014048]. - All four: Medicare negotiation rounds and government pricing agreements [CLM-008015] [CLM-008037].

docs.t: 2. Which partnerships create durable options Partner and deal ecosystem comparison
docs.x: Durable here means the structure leaves the company with a right but not an obligation, over several years, at bounded upfront cost. On the evidence: - AbbVie has the most option-type structures in the audited record, and its yearly early-stage upfronts run at USD 0.6bn to 1.0bn [CLM-009097] [CLM-009069]. - Takeda's Innovent arrangement combines a licence, equity and an option at USD 1.2bn upfront [CLM-009078]. - No option from the window has yet produced an approved product or an independent outcome, so durability is a (HYPOTHESIS) for all four companies. - Lilly's only data-for-access structure (TuneLab) creates an option on partner data and models, with no uptake result [CLM-009026] [CLM-014056].

docs.x: - Lilly: Catalyze360 bundles Lilly Ventures, Gateway Labs, ExploR&D and TuneLab; a USD 500m a16z fund is Lilly-funded; no stand-alone Lilly Ventures fund size was found; the CEO describes Gateway Labs as hosting "scale ups, not startups" and as an experiment that "may not work" [CLM-009025] [CLM-014063] [CLM-014068]. - J&J: JLABS was planned in 2016 at six sites with capacity for 225 companies; by August 2025 11 sites were active after exits from Toronto, Houston and Washington D.C., and a snippet says New York is closing, which would leave San Diego, San Francisco and Boston; no JJDC portfolio count is in primary sources [CLM-009051] [CLM-014064] [CLM-014065] [CLM-014066]. - AbbVie: AbbVie Ventures' founding is 2009 or about 2015 depending on the source (unresolved), and one source is sponsored content [CLM-009074] [CLM-009075]. - Takeda: no fund size or Center for External Innovation description in primary sources [CLM-014052].

docs.t: 4. Comparison validity Partner and deal ecosystem comparison
docs.x: - Deal values are not comparable across companies. The registry holds announced totals, consideration transferred, net-of-cash amounts, expensed IPR&D and upfronts for different deals. Examples: ImmunoGen 10.1 / 9.8 / 9.2bn; Morphic 3.2 / 2.55 / 3.35bn; Lilly IPR&D expense 2,910m versus cash paid 3,008m for FY2025 [CLM-003053] [CLM-009002] [CLM-000182] [CLM-000177]. - US GAAP versus IFRS. Asset acquisitions are expensed as acquired IPR&D at Lilly and AbbVie, so the same economic purchase appears as R&D expense for them; whether Takeda capitalises is not established (gap) [CLM-009095] [CLM-009098]. - Deal count is not capability. A9's own tables count rows, and for Takeda eight rows meet its target only by counting write-offs and divestitures [CLM-009098]. - Contract-term completeness differs. Lilly and AbbVie terms come from audited notes; J&J and Takeda licence terms are thin or undisclosed [CLM-009049] [CLM-009087].

docs.t: 2. Defined metrics and their validity R&D investment and productivity: what can and cannot be compared
docs.x: Metric Definition Computable for Valid for ranking? --- --- --- --- M1 R&D intensity R&D expense ÷ revenue, as reported all four (section 1.2) Partly. Currency-neutral, but R&D definitions differ (AbbVie includes impairments; J&J includes MedTech; Lilly excludes acquired IPR&D; Takeda IFRS). Use for direction of travel, not level M2 Window-cohort revenue share FY2025 revenue of molecules first approved after 2021-11-21 ÷ FY2025 revenue lower bounds for Lilly, J&J, AbbVie; not for Takeda No. Penalises lifecycle growth (see pipeline and revenue dependence.md) M3 Write-down ratio audited impairment ÷ net price of the acquisition it relates to AbbVie emraclidine only (54%) No. One data point; other companies' window-era impairments have different bases (programme-level, not deal-level) M4 Novel approvals ÷ cumulative R&D approvals counted 2021-11 to 2026-11 against R&D 2022-2025 counts exist; ratio rejected No , see below Why M4 is rejected. (1) The approval window runs to November 2026 and includes seven approvals dated 2026 (Lilly's Foundayo and Onswik, J&J's Icotyde, AbbVie's Decnupaz and Juvmo, Takeda's Orzeyful and Mimrylo) that were funded largely by spending before and after the 2022-2025 window rather than by that spend alone [CLM-012006] [CLM-012007] [CLM-012012] [CLM-012016] [CLM-012017] [CLM-012019] [CLM-012020]. Isomorphic (USD 45 million upfront, up to USD 1.7 billion) [CLM-006012]; insitro ADMET models [CLM-006009]; Chai custom antibody model (trade report) [CLM-006010]; OpenAI antimicrobials, announced June 2024, not September 2025 as the brief states [CLM-006011]. Maturity: concept to prototype. - Physical. Lebanon Advanced Therapies opened 2026-05-06 with robotic dosing/sealing seen on a tour [CLM-006002]; the USD 4.5 billion Medicine Foundry remains planned for late 2027 [CLM-006000, CLM-006001]. NVIDIA describes plant robots and digital twins without counts [CLM-006006]. Lilly's capex was USD 7.8 billion in 2025 [CLM-000246]. - Retreat. The Life Sciences Studio / Strateos remote robotic lab was sold to Arctoris in 2024 [CLM-006013]; a reported USD 90 million build cost conflicts with another source on dates [CLM-006014]. Contested: the reason for divesting the lab [CLM-006017]; whether Strateos closed or was acquired [CLM-006015]; the Chai hit-rate claim [CLM-006010]. Unknown: any result from LillyPod, TuneLab uptake, co-innovation lab status (concept at CLM-000281), Lilly Gateway Labs/Catalyze360 outcomes (not assessed), and Lilly's 10-K quantifies no AI outcome [CLM-000252].

docs.t: Autonomous Lab Reality Check (A6, wave 1) Autonomous Lab Reality Check (A6, wave 1)
docs.x: Question: what is technically and commercially mature today in laboratory automation and "autonomous" (closed-loop, AI-directed) discovery, judged only by evidence opened for this review? Cutoff 2026-11-21.

docs.t: What is established Autonomous Lab Reality Check (A6, wave 1)
docs.x: - Lilly built and then divested an open robotic cloud lab. The Life Sciences Studio in San Diego (public launch about 2020, with Strateos) was acquired by Arctoris in 2024 and relocated to Oxford, with five biochemistry modules, a high-throughput screening module, a BSL2 cell-biology module and storage for 4 million compounds [CLM-006013]. Cost (USD 90 million) and start year (2017 versus about 2020) are reported inconsistently [CLM-006014]. No disclosed discovery outcome came from it in any source opened. - The asset continues as a service. Arctoris (a CRO) runs the platform, expanded its biophysics capacity ten-fold and was selected for a UK ARIA AI Scientist programme [CLM-006016]. Automation is being sold as data generation for AI customers, not as an autonomous discovery engine. - Biofoundry automation plus ML did not guarantee commercial success. Zymergen sold to Ginkgo for about USD 300 million, one-tenth of its roughly USD 3 billion IPO-era valuation, after cumulative net losses of USD 1.2 billion and a discontinued first product [CLM-006051]. - Lilly's next step is an announcement. The NVIDIA–Lilly co-innovation lab (up to USD 1 billion over five years) targets a "continuous learning system" linking agentic wet labs with dry labs; it is at concept stage [CLM-000281]. LillyPod is operational as compute, with no reported result [CLM-006004, CLM-006007]. - Physical automation that is operating is conventional. The Lilly Lebanon Advanced Therapies plant has robotic machines that dose, measure and seal medicines, seen on a guided tour with no performance data [CLM-006002]. - A fast-feedback AI-wet-lab loop is claimed by vendors. Nabla says design-to-test takes three to four weeks and expects first-in-human data within one to two years (both company statements) [CLM-006039, CLM-006040]; BigHat pairs ML with a high-speed wet lab under an AbbVie deal with no result yet [CLM-006035].

docs.t: What is contested Autonomous Lab Reality Check (A6, wave 1)
docs.x: - Whether Lilly sold the Studio because the model failed, because utilisation was low or for portfolio reasons: the reason is undisclosed [CLM-006017]. - Whether Strateos closed or was acquired: one unverified aggregator snippet says it was acquired by Multiply Labs in December 2023; no primary source opened, so the research brief's "closure" is not confirmed [CLM-006015]. - Whether AI-originated molecules outperform conventional ones clinically. Rentosertib (Insilico) shows a peer-reviewed Phase IIa FVC signal with liver-safety discontinuations [CLM-006048]; Recursion ended four of 11 programmes in 2025 [CLM-006047]; the cited aggregate Phase 2 success rate for AI-originated compounds is about the same as conventional (secondary citation) [CLM-006049].

docs.t: What is unknown Autonomous Lab Reality Check (A6, wave 1)
docs.x: - Any peer-reviewed or audited result from a fully closed-loop autonomous lab at any of the four companies. - Utilisation, cost per experiment or error-rate data for Lilly's or any pharma's robotic labs. - Whether Lilly's co-innovation lab has begun operations. - Emerald Cloud Lab and other cloud-lab track records (not investigated).

docs.t: Technology readiness judgement (INTERPRETATION) Autonomous Lab Reality Check (A6, wave 1)
docs.x: Layer Readiness (evidence-based) Basis --- --- --- High-throughput, scripted automation (screening, dosing, fill-finish) operational, commodity Arctoris platform; Lilly plant [CLM-006013, CLM-006002] Remote/cloud access to a robotic lab operational but commercially fragile Studio divested; platform now CRO-run [CLM-006017, CLM-006016] AI-planned experiments in an owned wet-lab loop prototype to pilot, unproven Nabla/BigHat claims; co-innovation lab concept [CLM-006040, CLM-006035, CLM-000281] "Autonomous" end-to-end discovery with clinical outcome not demonstrated No source opened shows it

docs.t: Implications for Takeda (RECOMMENDATION) Autonomous Lab Reality Check (A6, wave 1)
docs.x: Rent automation and data generation (CRO model) rather than build an owned robotic lab; gate AI-biotech deals on first-in-human data; revisit when an independent outcome from Lilly's lab programme appears [CLM-006052, CLM-006058].

docs.t: What is established Launch execution evidence
docs.x: - Mounjaro/Zepbound : Mounjaro $22,965m (2024: $11,540m) and Zepbound $13,542m (2024: $4,926m); together 56% of Lilly revenue [CLM-007031] [CLM-001003]. Humira defence tactics: [CLM-003085]. - Carvykti : $1,887m vs $963m, attributed to share gains and capacity expansion, so supply governed pace [CLM-007029]. - Spravato : $1,696m vs $1,077m; distribution restricted to certified healthcare settings, no home dispensing [CLM-007029] [CLM-007030]. - Tremfya : $5,155m vs $3,670m; Crohn's approval March 2025 and Stelara-successor framing [CLM-007029] [CLM-002053]. - Kisunla : $21m in Q1 2025 (snippet only, source blocked) and $484m in 9M 2026 [CLM-007032] [CLM-001032]. docs.t: Pipeline quality and revenue-replacement assessment (INTERPRETATION) Pipeline quality and revenue-replacement assessment (INTERPRETATION)
docs.x: Everything below is analyst interpretation of the cited FACT claims, not a finding of fact.

docs.t: Depth Pipeline quality and revenue-replacement assessment (INTERPRETATION)
docs.x: - Lilly: eight CDER novel approvals plus the Zepbound NDA, and eight Phase 3 assets in the snapshot across incretin, lipoprotein(a), oncology and Alzheimer's [CLM-012000] [CLM-012021]. - J&J: five novel approvals (two bispecifics, an oral peptide, a TKI, an FcRn antibody) plus a bispecific/CAR-T oncology Phase 3 stack [CLM-012008] [CLM-012012]. - AbbVie: five novel approvals but the 2022-2025 growth came from Skyrizi/Rinvoq supplements [CLM-012033] [CLM-012036]; the 2023-2025 setbacks (ABBV-951 CRLs, emraclidine, navitoclax, VERONA) were larger in count than at peers [CLM-012116] [CLM-012117]. - Takeda: three novel approvals, all arriving in 2023 or 2026; two 2026 approvals plus zasocitinib Phase 3 form the replacement set [CLM-012019] [CLM-012131].

docs.t: Concentration Pipeline quality and revenue-replacement assessment (INTERPRETATION)
docs.x: - Lilly is the most concentrated: Mounjaro and Zepbound were 56% of 2025 revenue [CLM-012124], and the Phase 3 list is dominated by incretin and incretin-adjacent assets (retatrutide, orforglipron, eloralintide, tirzepatide outcomes). - J&J and AbbVie are concentrated in immunology (Tremfya, Skyrizi, Rinvoq) and oncology respectively; Stelara biosimilar erosion is described in J&J's FY2025 10-K (not registered as a claim; gap) and replacement sizing was not retrieved.

docs.t: Modality mix Pipeline quality and revenue-replacement assessment (INTERPRETATION)
docs.x: Broadest at J&J (bispecifics, CAR-T, oral peptide, drug-device, FcRn antibody) and AbbVie (ADCs, bispecific antibody, small molecules); Lilly spans peptides, oral small molecules and siRNA (lepodisiran) [CLM-012140]; Takeda spans oral small molecules, peptides, an siRNA and an antibody, having exited cell therapy [CLM-012123]. Gene editing and radioligand programmes were not evidenced.

docs.t: Revenue-replacement adequacy Pipeline quality and revenue-replacement assessment (INTERPRETATION)
docs.x: - Lilly: the pipeline mostly extends the franchise that already supplies the revenue (oral and multi-agonist incretins), so replacement need is low near term and the risk is concentration, not shortage; orforglipron's voucher and 2026-04-01 approval support timely launch [CLM-012125] [CLM-012006]. - J&J: Stelara is exposed to biosimilars; Tremfya, Icotyde and the bispecific/CAR-T stack are the identified successors, with Icotyde approved 2026-03-17 [CLM-012012]. Adequacy cannot be sized without revenue forecasts (gap). - AbbVie: Humira revenue fell sharply in 2025 and is offset by Skyrizi and Rinvoq (gap: the FY2025 10-K revenue table was read but not registered as a claim) ; the novel pipeline (tavapadon, ADCs) is smaller than the lost revenue, so growth depends on immunology supplements and label expansion (INTERPRETATION) ; Rinvoq GCA supplement [CLM-012036]. - Takeda: Exkivity withdrawal, Alofisel and cell-therapy impairments, and soticlestat failure removed several late assets [CLM-012121] [CLM-012120]; oveporexton and zasocitinib are the principal replacement bets. Confidence: moderate on counts and dates (regulator records), low on adequacy (no forecast data retrieved).

docs.t: Eli Lilly Scientific platform capabilities (evidence-based)
docs.x: - Lilly platform capability (oral small-molecule incretin chemistry): orforglipron is an oral GLP-1 receptor agonist that reached an FDA approval (Foundayo, 2026-04-01) and has an ATTAIN Phase 3 publication programme including a JAMA report in obstructive sleep apnea. (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012138] - Lilly platform capability (multi-agonist peptides): retatrutide, a GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, has Phase 2 (NEJM 2023) and TRIUMPH-1 Phase 3 (NEJM, 2026-11-05) publications and a 10,000-participant outcomes trial. (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012139] - Lilly platform capability (RNA therapeutics): lepodisiran, an siRNA against lipoprotein(a), is in the ACCLAIM-Lp(a) cardiovascular outcomes Phase 3 (registry record NCT06292013, about 17,300 participants). (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012140] - Lilly platform capability (precision oncology small molecules): Lilly (via Loxo Oncology) obtained FDA approval of Jaypirca in 2023 and converted CLL/SLL from accelerated to traditional approval on 2025-12-02, and Inluriyo was approved 2025-09-25. (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012141]

docs.t: Johnson & Johnson Scientific platform capabilities (evidence-based)
docs.x: - J&J platform capability (T-cell-engaging bispecifics): Tecvayli (2022-10-25) and Talvey (2023-08-09) were both approved by FDA, Tecvayli's pivotal MajesTEC-1 was published in NEJM, and MajesTEC-7 Phase 3 (NCT05552222) combines the two engagers. (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012142] - J&J platform capability (oral targeted peptides): icotrokinra, an oral IL-23 receptor peptide, was approved as Icotyde on 2026-03-17 and its Phase 3 results are published in NEJM (2025-11-06). (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012143] - J&J platform capability (CAR-T and bispecific oncology): cilta-cel CARTITUDE-4 was published in NEJM (2023-07-27) and CARTITUDE-5 Phase 3 (NCT04923893) has an estimated primary completion of 2029-02-14. (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012144] - J&J platform capability (EGFR/MET bispecific plus TKI combination): Rybrevant plus Lazcluze received first-line FDA approval on 2024-08-19 supported by MARIPOSA (NEJM 2024), and an OrigAMI-2 colorectal Phase 3 (NCT06662786) is recruiting. (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012145]

docs.t: AbbVie Scientific platform capabilities (evidence-based)
docs.x: - AbbVie platform capability (antibody-drug conjugates): FDA records show Elahere (2022-11-14, sponsor ImmunoGen) and Emrelis (2025-05-14, AbbVie) approvals, Decnupaz (2026-05-27) approval, and a Temab-A Phase 2/3 with osimertinib (NCT07005102). (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012146] - AbbVie platform capability (immunology lifecycle management): FDA approved Skyrizi in Crohn's disease (2022-06-16) and ulcerative colitis (2024-06-18) and Rinvoq in atopic dermatitis (2022-01-14), ulcerative colitis (2022-03-16) and giant cell arteritis (2025-04-28). (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012147] - AbbVie neuroscience capability: tavapadon (D1/D5 partial agonist) has a published fixed-dose Phase 3 (JAMA Neurol 2026), an NDA submitted September 2025 and FDA approval as Juvmo on 2026-09-25, while emraclidine failed Phase 2. (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012148]

docs.t: Takeda Scientific platform capabilities (evidence-based)
docs.x: - Takeda platform capability (orexin biology): oveporexton, an oral orexin-2 agonist, has NEJM Phase 2 (2025) and Phase 3 (2026-09-24) publications and was approved as Orzeyful on 2026-08-05. (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012149] - Takeda platform capability (oral TYK2 inhibition): zasocitinib has a Phase 2 publication (JAMA Dermatol 2024), two completed Phase 3 psoriasis registry entries, and a completed head-to-head Phase 3 versus deucravacitinib (NCT06973291). (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012150] - Takeda platform capability (in-licensed first-in-class assets): rusfertide (hepcidin mimetic, Protagonist) has a Phase 3 VERIFY publication in J Clin Oncol (2026-10) and FDA approval as Mimrylo on 2026-08-28. (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012151] - Takeda platform capability (RNAi): fazirsiran, a GalNAc siRNA, is in Phase 3 for alpha-1 antitrypsin liver disease (NCT05677971, primary completion estimated 2029-01-17). (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-012152] Not evidenced in this run (gap): Lilly radioligand (POINT) and gene editing (Verve), J&J ADC via Ambrx and Legend relationship detail, AbbVie in-vivo CAR-T (Capstan), Takeda cell-therapy exit rationale beyond the impairment disclosure [CLM-012123].

docs.t: 1. Lilly: earnings 8-K exhibits (Q4 2025, Q3 2026) A14 gap-fill findings (wave 2)
docs.x: Established - Lilly's Q4 2025 release (8-K Ex. 99.1, filed 2026-02-04) reports FY2025 revenue of USD 65,179m (+45%): Mounjaro USD 22,965m, Zepbound USD 13,542m, Verzenio USD 5,723m. [CLM-014000] - FY2025 R&D was USD 13,337m and acquired IPR&D USD 2,910m. Q4 2025 realized price fell 5% while volume rose 46%. [CLM-014004] - Initial 2026 guidance was revenue USD 80-83bn, non-GAAP EPS USD 33.50-35.00 and performance margin 46.0-47.5%. [CLM-014001] - The brief's "USD 91-92bn" is the raised guidance in the Q3 2026 release (2026-10-29), which lifted the revenue midpoint by USD 5.5bn from USD 85-87bn. Q3 2026 revenue was USD 24,397m (+39%). [CLM-014002] - Q3 2026 revenue included about USD 900m of one-off benefits (USD 410m Jardiance milestones, rebate/discount estimate adjustments). Realized price fell 15% and volume rose 53%. [CLM-014003] - The 10-K (not the 8-K) is the only filed source that quantifies LillyDirect: self-pay sales through LillyDirect were "a growing portion" of 2025 business, with no dollar figure. [CLM-014006] - Neither earnings exhibit contains LillyDirect, self-pay, OSA or HFpEF statements. [CLM-014005] - Zepbound/Mounjaro OSA is recorded as "approved in the U.S. and the EU in 2024" and HFpEF as "submitted in 2024"; the FY2025 10-K shows HFpEF "approved in the EU" only. [CLM-014007] Contested / unknown : exact FDA action dates for OSA and the U.S. HFpEF outcome (gap) . Q3/9M 2026 are partial periods. Integrate into: New mediciine/companies/eli lilly/ dossier §2 (financials) and §4 (commercial/access); correct any "USD 91-92bn" attribution to "raised in Q3 2026 (Oct 29, 2026); initial Feb 2026 guidance USD 80-83bn".

docs.t: 3. J&J: Varipulse, aticaprant, DePuy Synthes separation, OTTAVA/MONARCH/VELYS, talc A14 gap-fill findings (wave 2)
docs.x: Varipulse. FDA's correction notice: approved November 2024; 4 of 132 patients (about 3%) in the U.S. External Evaluation had stroke/TIA versus about 1% expected; Instructions for Use updated 2025-02-14 for all lots (most serious recall class, correction not removal); a post-approval study is planned. [CLM-014018] Aticaprant. J&J discontinued the Phase 3 VENTURA programme on 2025-03-06 for insufficient efficacy; safety was acceptable. [CLM-014019] DePuy Synthes. Intent to separate Orthopaedics announced 2025-10-14 (FY2024 sales about USD 9.2bn; Namal Nawana named Worldwide President). [CLM-014020] The 10-K targets completion 18-24 months after announcement; Orthopaedics FY2025 sales were USD 9.3bn (+1.1%). [CLM-014022] - First IDE cases were early 2025; a hernia IDE was approved late 2025. [CLM-014023] - The first early-access commercial installation was announced 2026-11-19. [CLM-014024] - Duato had guided approval "by the end of this year, beginning of next year"; FDA acted earlier. docs.x: Source of the challenges: decision memo to director.md, council reviews.md (119 verdicts: 45 support / 64 conditional / 10 oppose; 17 recorded disagreements), red team.md, scenario stress test.md, counterarguments and uncertainty.md (95 items). This record is authoritative for strategy v2. The v1 strategy files (A11c) are revised to match it by the A11c-bis pass; the deliverables cite v2. Nothing here is a reported fact about Takeda: every number is an ASSUMPTION or a council computation and is labelled as such in the strategy data. Council proposal Director decision Rationale (evidence or assumption) --- --- --- --- 1 BET-15 (USD 5bn+ asset purchase, DEFER) → REJECT as framed; create a funded USD 0.5–2bn Phase 2/3 licensing channel (BET-18) ACCEPTED. BET-15 → REJECT. Add BET-18 "Phase 2/3 in-licensing channel" as PARTNER/INVEST, sized USD 0.5–2bn contingent on IVB-012 (Amitiza cash) and the leverage ceiling (ASM-033). The council's leverage arithmetic (2.6x → ~3.1–3.4x) breaks the strategy's own 3.0x ceiling; Takeda's observed pattern is mid-size licensing (Nimbus USD 4.0bn upfront, Innovent USD 1.2bn upfront — A9/A5 claims). BET-18 is council-proposed: its A–M template is completed by A11c-bis and labelled "v2 addition". 2 Widen ASM-025 (Entyvio biosimilar entry) from 2030–32 to 2028–32; add early-entry stress case; move RM-026 to 2028 H1 ACCEPTED. Two biosimilar BLAs under FDA review (A14 CLM-014051); exclusivity timing outside the registry (IVB-004 remains open). No extra capital. 3 BET-06 option engine: balanced USD 700m → constrained USD 300m, scorecard-first, balance contingent ACCEPTED. Commercial and capital councils oppose at USD 700m; option conversion rate is an unvalidated assumption (ASM-028). 4 BET-02 plasma: BUILD → EXPERIMENT (baseline + shadow-mode tranche); re-base ASM-031; add demand-vs-capacity and plasma-peer tests ACCEPTED (Takeda-execution council's dissent recorded). PDT revenue −1.5% CER does not show a capacity constraint (A5); no fixed-price vendor evidence; "unique data" rests on an absent peer

docs.x: Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Independent challenge by a fresh-context agent. Claim IDs were re-checked against claims registry.jsonl , including correction , contrary evidence and status fields. Takeda fiscal years run April-March (FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026). Bet decisions are those in strategy/data/strategy bets.json ; this file does not change them. How to read the verdicts. A verdict is the council's stance on the proposed decision as recorded (BUILD, INVEST, PARTNER, EXPERIMENT, DEFER or REJECT). support backs the decision as written. conditional backs it only if the stated condition is met. oppose disputes the decision or its sizing. For REJECT and DEFER bets, support means the council endorses the REJECT or DEFER, and the rationale begins 'Endorses'. Councils were run independently and their disagreements are recorded in the log below, not averaged away. Dollar figures are the strategy's ASSUMPTIONs (ASM-002 to ASM-004, ASM-101 to ASM-117); Takeda's budget is not public (IVB-014). Claim-quality findings that apply to every council (re-checked against the registry): - Of 215 distinct claim IDs cited by the 17 bets, 134 are SUPPORTED, 57 PARTIALLY SUPPORTED, 17 NEEDS MORE RESEARCH and 7 INCONCLUSIVE. The NEEDS MORE RESEARCH claims are mostly the registry's own HYPOTHESIS entries for the AI, plasma, orexin, registry and launch-pathway bets (CLM-011027 to CLM-011081), so those bets cite hypotheses as evidence. - Six bets (BET-04, 05, 08, 09, 11, 16) are labelled evidence backed although a load-bearing claim is PARTIALLY SUPPORTED or NEEDS MORE RESEARCH (for example CLM-007053 for BET-11, CLM-011065 and CLM-011066 for BET-09, CLM-011054 for BET-08). - Known errors that remain in the strategy text: 'CVS removed Zepbound for about 11 months [CLM-007011]' (the claim records an 11% share-price fall; CVS restored Zepbound from 1 October 2026 per CLM-007013, about 15 months); stage-gate capital at risk exceeds the bet size by USD

[CLM-011017] [CLM-003002] (ASM-024) - CA-002 (THEME). ASM-025 puts first meaningful US Entyvio biosimilar entry at 2031 (range 2030-2032). The range excludes entry in 2027-2029. Under the statutory 12-year reference-product exclusivity (a rule outside the registry, to be verified), the regulatory barrier would already have lapsed in May 2026, leaving patents as the only barrier. First-entry erosion is a US event, so the three-year window is overstated on the global base, while ex-US erosion follows later and is absent from the table. docs.x: Research cutoff 2026-11-21. From: independent Strategic Council and red team (A11e). To: Director. The council reviewed all 17 bets in strategy/data/strategy bets.json with seven councils (scientific, technology, commercial, capital allocation, regulatory and ethics, competitive red team, Takeda execution). Details: council reviews.md, red team.md, scenario stress test.md, counterarguments and uncertainty.md. Bets, portfolios and roadmap were not edited; every change below is a proposal. docs.t: 1. Summary Decision memo to the Director: proposed changes to the 17 bets (A11e, wave 5)
docs.x: Over 119 reviews the councils returned 45 support, 64 conditional and 10 oppose. The decisions the councils back without material change are BET-05, BET-08, BET-09, BET-10, BET-14, BET-16 and, with conditions, BET-01 and BET-17. Ten changes are proposed, ranked by consequence for the Entyvio window (2031-2034 under ASM-025) and strength of evidence. Headline finding. The portfolio spends 49.5% of its balanced envelope (USD 1,460m of 2,950m: BET-03, 06, 07 and 13) on bets whose own evaluation puts payoff at eight years or more, after the Entyvio erosion window, while the instrument Takeda has actually used to refill its pipeline (mid-size Phase 2/3 licences: Nimbus USD 4.0bn, Innovent USD 1.2bn upfront, Protagonist, Keros, Arrowhead) has no funded bet. Four of six late-stage programmes were externally sourced [CLM-005050] [CLM-009076] [CLM-009078]. BET-15 (USD 5bn or more) is the only bridge in the set and fails the strategy's own leverage test by arithmetic.

docs.t: BET-01 Governed cross-franchise R&D data and decision layer (BUILD; exposure MEDIUM) Red team: the strongest case against each bet (A11e, wave 5)
docs.x: Strongest case against. A governance layer over a platform Takeda says it already has (a Databricks agent platform for 10,000+ employees, insourced digital factories) duplicates existing spend and will be judged by usage counts, the same failure visible in J&J's 47,000 course completions. No data layer at any company has an independent outcome, and the only Takeda outcome claim (about 30% shorter narcolepsy trial development) is one executive interview. If Takeda's estate is already governed, the incremental value is near zero and USD 200m is a sunk platform that is hard to stop. Evidence. No independent outcome for ARCH, TuneLab, Polyphonic or the AISB model; the 'fragmented estate' premise is a NEEDS MORE RESEARCH hypothesis; platform maturity is vendor self-report; 63.4% workforce use is an adoption metric. [CLM-011052] [CLM-011055] [CLM-005058] [CLM-014073] [CLM-014043] [CLM-006022] What would have to be true for the bet to survive. - IVB-001 shows production use is thin or fragmented, not already governed. - Two decisions can be baselined before any model is applied. - A second function adopts the standard within 12 months. Kill criteria. - No decision baselined by 2027 H2 (the bet's own test), then stop and redirect to BET-08. - Gate 3 (RM-015, 2027 H2) shows zero of two decisions with a measured effect on cycle time, hit rate or cost. - Run cost exceeds measured benefit at scale gate.

docs.t: BET-02 Plasma process-intelligence and fixed-price automation programme (BUILD; exposure HIGH) Red team: the strongest case against each bet (A11e, wave 5)
docs.x: Strongest case against. The thesis rests on three unproven links: that plasma is capacity-bound (but H1 FY2026 PDT revenue was -1.5% at constant rates), that Takeda's process data are unique (the comparison set has no plasma peers), and that a fixed-price outcome-linked automation vendor exists (NEEDS MORE RESEARCH; the SpaceX source says its cost gap is not isolated and every cargo partner had catastrophic failures). Takeda has no public robotics evidence, a prior warning letter and shortage, and USD 230m of expansion without commissioning data. The follow-on of USD 350m is committed on a 2% threshold that has no economic anchor. Evidence. PDT revenue +8.5% AER and -1.5% CER; no yield or productivity figures; no evidence of manufacturing robotics; Hikari warning letter with a USD 505m award; plasma peers (CSL, Grifols, Octapharma and others) are not in the registry. [CLM-005064] [CLM-005060] [CLM-005067] [CLM-005020] [CLM-011031] [CLM-011006] [CLM-011008] [CLM-005065] What would have to be true for the bet to survive. - IVB-006 shows yield or cost headroom above the pilot threshold that matters in money terms (ASM-031 must be re-based on cost per litre). - At least one vendor prices fixed-price, outcome-linked terms for GMP automation. - Validated change control does not trigger new inspection observations. - Plasma is capacity-bound, so lower cost per litre converts to revenue. Kill criteria. - Baseline headroom below ASM-031 (re-based) by 2027 H2. - No vendor accepts outcome-linked terms at feasibility. - Any new inspection observation attributable to the pilot. - PDT revenue stays flat or negative at CER after the Los Angeles capacity is commissioned (signals demand-bound).

Second-asset approval is a 5-30% proposition by the strategy's own range, payoff is 2038, and USD 500m is 17% of the balanced envelope. A platform does not protect a product (EYLEA -42% in 2025). Meanwhile the Entyvio window opens in 2031 and the capital arrives after it. An orexin discovery team already sits in base R&D, so the incremental USD 500m may fund work that would happen anyway. Evidence. ASM-021 15%; RM-048 platform test 2038; TAK-994 liver signal; soticlestat Phase 3 miss and JPY 21.5bn impairment; no competitor orexin review; EYLEA -42%. [CLM-005023] [CLM-012119] [CLM-012120] [CLM-009083] [CLM-011017] [CLM-011037] [CLM-005025] What would have to be true for the bet to survive. - A second orexin asset with a clean safety profile exists by 2028. - Competitors have no faster follower in the same indications. - The USD 500m is additive to the Shonan base budget. Kill criteria. - No second target clears safety by gate 1 (2028). - IND-enabling package incomplete by 2031 (RM-030 target H1 2030). - Phase 2 fails on placebo response or exposure (LES-18). - Single approval only after 2040: withdraw the platform claim.

docs.t: BET-04 Entyvio franchise defence: payer contracting, evidence and lifecycle (BUILD; exposure MEDIUM) Red team: the strongest case against each bet (A11e, wave 5)
docs.x: Strongest case against. Humira is the best analogue and it argues against the premise: rebate-for-access held at least 97% of volume for 14 months, a co-brand route followed, and global Humira still fell 78.6% in three years. AbbVie and J&J already sell competing IBD products, and PBMs now prefer their own biosimilars (CVS Stelara template, July 2026). The January 2028 Medicare price is statutory and cannot be contracted away. Contracting levers work in the pharmacy benefit; Entyvio IV may largely sit outside it (not in the registry). USD 140m will not change an exposure of JPY 383-766bn a year, so the real risk is that the programme is a visible reassurance with no measurable lever. Evidence. Humira -78.6% 2022-2025; US Humira -41% (2024) and -57% (2025); Skyrizi, Rinvoq and Tremfya hold IBD approvals; four of nine Stelara biosimilars are PBM-affiliated private labels; Entyvio selected for Medicare negotiation. docs.t: BET-11 Drug-device and home/SC administration platform (BUILD; exposure MEDIUM) Red team: the strongest case against each bet (A11e, wave 5)
docs.x: Strongest case against. SC is table stakes: Tremfya, Skyrizi and Rinvoq are already convenient, and the biosimilars in review are IV. SC moves Entyvio patients into the pharmacy benefit, where PBM private-label biosimilar templates operate, so the pen could accelerate erosion after entry. Device IP does not outlive the drug's own protection, and Takeda has not shown persistence data. Evidence. CLM-007053 is PARTIALLY SUPPORTED yet the bet is labelled evidence backed; PBM template from 1 July 2026; four of nine Stelara biosimilars are PBM-affiliated. [CLM-007053] [CLM-007015] [CLM-007016] [CLM-014051] [CLM-007042] [CLM-002026] What would have to be true for the bet to survive. - SC users persist better after biosimilar entry than IV users. - SC does not cannibalise IV before exclusivity loss. Kill criteria. - SC erodes net price faster than it retains patients (stage-gate stop). - No retention effect after entry (RM-040, 2033). - Device recall or clearance setback.

docs.t: BET-12 Launch-pathway partnerships and patient-services outcome measurement (EXPERIMENT; exposure MEDIUM) Red team: the strongest case against each bet (A11e, wave 5)
docs.x: Strongest case against. No company publishes persistence or time-to-therapy outcomes, so the bet has no benchmark and the hypothesis that pathways govern launch speed is untested. Oveporexton was approved on 2026-08-05; the pilot starts in 2027 H2 and reports in 2028 H2, after the launch curve forms. Pear's failure shows payers, not evidence, decide. Evidence. Help at Hand is an enrolment count; Spravato and Carvykti constraints were certification and capacity; AbbVie's Allē change reversed within months. [CLM-007039] [CLM-007037] [CLM-011070] [CLM-007045] [CLM-007046] [CLM-003033] [CLM-005029] What would have to be true for the bet to survive. - Oveporexton uptake is pathway-limited. - Hub data can be owned and measured. Kill criteria. - No pathway bottleneck identified at the prototype gate. - No improvement in time to first dose in the pilot. - Any compliance finding.

Flatiron regulatory-use claim is a vendor snippet; no Takeda network. [CLM-011022] [CLM-011049] [CLM-011050] [CLM-011023] [CLM-005072] What would have to be true for the bet to survive. - A neutral sponsor and patient-organisation partners exist. [CLM-006008] [CLM-009027] [CLM-011004] [CLM-000280] What would have to be true for the bet to survive. - A measured Takeda advantage and external demand. docs.t: BET-15 Large asset purchase (USD 5bn or more) as LOE bridge (DEFER; exposure MEDIUM) Red team: the strongest case against each bet (A11e, wave 5)
docs.x: Strongest case against. (Attack on the DEFER.) Both ways. If Takeda waits for 2031 triggers, AbbVie and J&J have already bought bridges (USD 17.5bn net each in 2024 and 2025) and the best Phase 2/3 assets are gone. If Takeda buys at USD 5bn, adjusted leverage is about 3.1x before Amitiza and about 3.4x with it, against a 3.0x ceiling the strategy itself set, and a Cerevel-type write-down (54% of price) would be JPY 400bn. The binary USD 5bn framing leaves the middle (USD 0.5-2bn licences, the Nimbus and Innovent pattern) unfunded. Evidence. Leverage 2.6x at March 2026; Amitiza provision JPY 403.5bn; progressive dividend JPY 313.2bn paid in FY2025; no significant acquisitions in three years. [CLM-005005] [CLM-005014] [CLM-005006] [CLM-003086] [CLM-009049] [CLM-009054] [CLM-009087] What would have to be true for the bet to survive. - Free cash flow after dividends deleverages Takeda below the ceiling within 24 months. - A named Phase 2+ asset passes the write-down test. Kill criteria. - Any unmet trigger: no deal (the bet's own rule). - Leverage above 3.0x after Amitiza clarity: remove BET-15 from the roadmap.

TrumpRx agreements expire with the presidential term; Takeda's status is not in the registry. [CLM-007009] [CLM-008037] [CLM-007010] [CLM-007052] What would have to be true for the bet to survive. - Takeda's categories stay specialty. Kill criteria. - A Takeda pricing agreement that requires a direct channel: reopen.

docs.t: BET-17 AI use-case measurement, decision support and reskilling (EXPERIMENT; exposure LOW) Red team: the strongest case against each bet (A11e, wave 5)
docs.x: Strongest case against. The bet can become a reporting ritual. Measurement is owned by the CFO who owns the JPY 200bn savings target, role cuts are proceeding in parallel, and J&J's own numbers (10-15% of use cases drive 80% of value) come from one interview. The reskilling plan needs credibility with employees who are losing roles. Evidence. J&J metrics are self-reported; Takeda 63.4% is usage; the savings target mixes technology with headcount. [CLM-006019] [CLM-006020] [CLM-006022] [CLM-014043] [CLM-005059] [CLM-005078] What would have to be true for the bet to survive. - Baselines can be set per use case. - Measurement is independent of the savings owner. Kill criteria. - No baseline for a use case: stop that use case (stage gate). - At the FY2028 checkpoint (RM-023) technology share of savings cannot be separated.

The strategy's robustness table is reproduced and re-rated by the council. Where the council differs the cell is marked and the reason is given. Capital figures are the strategy's balanced-portfolio ASSUMPTIONs (cumulative 2027-2040, USD m); Takeda's budget is not public (IVB-014). Council arithmetic is derived from registry values and ASM-001 (JPY 150 per USD).

docs.t: 1. Scenario recap and what each stresses Scenario stress test (A11e, wave 5)
docs.x: - SCN-1 AI materially accelerates R&D. SCENARIO: by about 2031 independent evidence shows AI-planned discovery and development cutting cycle time or raising hit rate at several companies; first-in-human data from AI-designed molecules are positive; compute and models commoditise further. - SCN-2 AI incremental. SCENARIO: AI delivers productivity gains in documents, operations and decision support but no step change in probability of success or cycle time; no independent outcome appears for platform investments. - SCN-3 Pricing, regulatory and biosimilar pressure intensifies. SCENARIO: Medicare negotiation, most-favoured-nation pricing and PBM private-label biosimilars compress net price faster; Entyvio erosion lands at the high end of ASM-024; Takhzyro and others face negotiated prices. - SCN-4 New modalities, care models and tech-native competitors reshape value. SCENARIO: in-vivo cell therapy, siRNA and gene editing move into the clinic; home and digital care models change where value accrues; AI-native biotechs and tech platforms (Isomorphic-type) win partnerships; platforms do not protect single products. - SCN-5 Combined downside. SCENARIO: SCN-2 and SCN-3 together, plus launch slippage for 2026 approvals (inspection findings, payer delays) and Amitiza cash outflow near the full provision; leverage stays near 3x and discretionary spend is cut.

For ten counterpart types this file gives the competitor precedent and outcome evidence (A9, A6), Takeda's observed pattern (A5 baseline), and a suggested mode. Modes are options, labelled EVIDENCE BACKED (follows from outcome evidence) or HYPOTHESIS (reasoned; needs non-public data). They are not endorsements. docs.t: Reading the modes Partnership models: build, partner, license, acquire or invest (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: - Build : develop internally. Partner : collaboration without ownership transfer. License : pay for rights (upfront, milestones, royalties). Acquire : buy the company or asset. Invest : minority equity, funds or venture creation. - Outcome evidence is thin: most AI and automation deals have no disclosed result [CLM-006007, CLM-006045]; value destruction concentrates in neuroscience, gene and cell therapy and robotics [CLM-009100].

docs.t: Where the choice of mode changes the economics (INTERPRETATION) Partnership models: build, partner, license, acquire or invest (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: - Licence and option payments are mostly contingent: Takeda's AI deals carry over USD 1bn and USD 1.7bn of success-based payments that cost nothing unless data are positive [CLM-006039, CLM-006041]. Acquisitions put cash up front and expose write-down: AbbVie wrote off about 54% of Cerevel's net price [CLM-009054]. - Contingent value rights and sales milestones are used to share risk (Prevail, Akouos, Verve, Abiomed, Nimbus) [CLM-009099]. - A neutral platform (Flatiron) preserves customer base; owner-led platforms (TuneLab) may deter rivals from contributing, but TuneLab and AISB show rivals will join federated models [CLM-011022, CLM-006056].

docs.t: Stage gates (A11c v2, wave 6) Stage gates (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: Version v2 (A11c-bis, 2026-11-21). Gate capital is allocated in whole USD 5m units that sum to the bet size, so no bet's gates exceed its size. Each material bet moves discovery - feasibility - prototype - controlled pilot - scale decision - ongoing value review. Capital at risk is the balanced-portfolio capital committed between that gate and the next (USD m, ASSUMPTION ASM-037 shares of the balanced total; BET-02 and BET-18 use the explicit gate amounts shown in the JSON capital at risk usd m ; BET-18 gates draw on its contingent pool, not on committed capital). Owner and authority are roles, not named persons; the delegated limits are not public and are an ASSUMPTION. Shorter gate lists (BET-05, 08, 12, 13, 17, 18) use the stage names that apply and the shares in the JSON. REJECT bets (BET-10, 14, 15, 16) have no gates; BET-10 and BET-14 are governed by the ladder triggers in BET-09 and the roadmap. Rules that apply to every gate. (1) A gate decision is made on the evidence listed, not on spend to date. (2) A missed stop criterion ends or redirects the bet unless the decision authority records a reason in writing (RECOMMENDATION). (3) Expansion releases the next tranche only; no tranche is pre-committed beyond the portfolio horizon. (4) Evidence is reviewed against a baseline set at the preceding gate, so usage or enrolment counts do not substitute for outcomes [CLM-006022] [CLM-007039].

docs.t: Domain 1: Data advantage (A11b, wave 3) Domain 1: Data advantage (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda fiscal years run April-March (FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026). Options are labelled EVIDENCE BACKED (follows from cited evidence) or HYPOTHESIS (reasoned, needs non-public data). Nothing here is an endorsement. Baseline class numbers refer to capability baseline.md. Problem addressed: drug discovery and development decisions depend on proprietary experimental, clinical and real-world data that is fragmented inside each company and too sparse in public sources for drug-like targets. (INTERPRETATION)

docs.t: What the evidence shows Domain 1: Data advantage (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Deployed versus announced (competitors) - Lilly TuneLab is live: launched 2025-09-09, Lilly-trained models offered to biotechs with federated learning, underlying data cost estimated by Lilly at over USD 1 billion [CLM-000280]. Distribution through Benchling (1,300+ customers) is opt-in "later this year", with no uptake figure [CLM-006008]. A vendor blog reports over 2 million Lilly and 675,000 partner data points as of October 2026 (single vendor source) [CLM-009028]. Maturity: operational platform, pilot distribution, no independent outcome [CLM-006007]. - AbbVie ARCH is operational: conceived 2020, built by fewer than ten full-time staff plus contractors over a 124 TB corpus, and governance opened de-identified data from 2,000+ clinical trials to all R&D [CLM-006032, CLM-006034]. Outcome evidence is a preprint not opened by A6. - J&J Polyphonic is early access to select hospitals; the Abu Dhabi network is "expected" [CLM-006030, CLM-006031]. Maturity: pilot and concept. - Five companies (AbbVie, Astex, BMS, J&J, Takeda) fine-tuned OpenFold3 on over 20,000 private structures; the organiser reports about 10 points better pose accuracy than the best public model on 1,056 held-out structures, not peer reviewed [CLM-006043]. Takeda is not on the AISB Bind founding list [CLM-006044]. - Across these four assets, none has independent outcome evidence [CLM-011052]. Takeda baseline - Public evidence is a platform and an aspiration: a Databricks-hosted agent platform for 10,000+ employees (vendor-hosted, partly supported) [CLM-005058], 80% external digital workforce when the transformation was designed [CLM-005057], a stated aim to embed AI in every stage of discovery [CLM-005053], and no quantified outcome [CLM-006045, CLM-011053]. Contrary evidence - NVIDIA states that customers with in-house capability can replace platform layers [CLM-011004], which applies to data platforms too (INTERPRETATION) . The A10 audit also marks the AISB result as vendor-organised and the CIO-reported J&J metrics as self-reported [CLM-006020].

docs.t: Where proprietary advantage exists Domain 1: Data advantage (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: - Proprietary experimental data generated over decades is the one defensible asset; compute and third-party models are purchasable by rivals [CLM-006055]. - Advantage is strongest where data is expensive to regenerate (company-estimated over USD 1 billion for TuneLab) and where partners add data back, strengthening the model (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-011082, CLM-011087]. - Open standards or partnering fit better for public-like tasks (structure prediction, ADMET baselines) where no single company has enough data; federated consortia are the common mechanism [CLM-006056].

Evidence requirements: a data investment is justified only by a measured change in cycle time, hit rate or cost per decision, none of which Takeda or any competitor has published.

docs.t: Success criteria Domain 1: Data advantage (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: - Production inventory of data and AI products with users and outcomes (closes IVB-001). - A named decision (target selection, trial design, supply planning) where a model changed the outcome, with a pre-agreed baseline (HYPOTHESIS) . - Federated model gains on Takeda held-out data versus public models, reported with the organiser's method disclosed (HYPOTHESIS) .

docs.t: Risks Domain 1: Data advantage (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: - Regulatory: FDA's January 2025 draft guidance proposes a risk-based credibility framework for AI used in regulatory decisions, so model evidence must be documented [CLM-006046]. - Data and liability: Takeda's 20-F warns AI models may be flawed or trained on inadequate data [CLM-005054]. - Privacy and consent limit pooling; federation reduces but does not remove this (INTERPRETATION) . - Platform lock-in: a competitor-led federated platform strengthens that competitor's models as partners contribute [CLM-006055].

docs.t: Evidence and gaps Domain 1: Data advantage (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Gaps: internal AI inventory (IVB-001), TuneLab uptake, ARCH outcomes, Takeda data estate, plasma yield data (IVB-006). Details in evidence gaps.md.

docs.t: Domain 2: Next-generation R&D (A11b, wave 3) Domain 2: Next-generation R&D (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026. Options are labelled EVIDENCE BACKED or HYPOTHESIS; none is an endorsement. Baseline classes are from capability baseline.md. Problem addressed: replace revenue lost to patent expiry with new molecules faster and with a higher probability of success, using new modalities and computational design. (INTERPRETATION)

docs.t: What the evidence shows Domain 2: Next-generation R&D (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: AI-enabled discovery: deployed versus announced - Lilly: Isomorphic collaboration (USD 45 million upfront, up to USD 1.7 billion milestones, 2024-01-07) is at concept stage [CLM-006012]; the Chai custom antibody model is a trade report and Chai's hit-rate claim is Chai's own [CLM-006010]; no candidate is named in any opened source [CLM-006007]. - AbbVie: BigHat (USD 30 million upfront) at prototype and Valkai at concept [CLM-006035, CLM-006037]. - Takeda: Nabla Bio second collaboration (October 2025; double-digit millions upfront, over USD 1 billion success-based) with first-in-human data expected in one to two years, and Iambic (February 2026, success-based payments could exceed USD 1.7 billion) [CLM-006039, CLM-006041]. Nabla states a three to four week design-to-test loop, a company claim [CLM-006040]. All are prototype or earlier [CLM-006045]. - Outcome evidence from the wider industry is limited and mixed: Recursion ended four of 11 programmes in 2025 [CLM-006047]; Insilico's rentosertib Phase IIa (71 patients) showed +98.4 mL FVC at 60 mg with seven discontinuations for liver injury [CLM-006048]; AI-origin Phase 2 success is cited as about the same as conventional (secondary citation) [CLM-006049]. Synthesis: [CLM-011057]. New modalities: acquired or optioned, not built - AbbVie: Capstan (in vivo CAR-T, USD 2.1 billion) and the ADARx siRNA option (USD 335 million upfront, up to USD 7.5 billion milestones) [CLM-009058, CLM-009061]. Lilly: Verve (gene editing) and POINT (radioligands) [CLM-009010, CLM-009006]. J&J: Ambrx (ADC) and Halda [CLM-009035, CLM-009032]. Maturity: early clinical or concept; outcomes not yet visible [CLM-011059]. Takeda's route to date - Window approvals came from conventional routes: oveporexton from in-house orexin science (approved 2026-08-05), rusfertide from Protagonist (approved 2026-08-28), zasocitinib via the Nimbus purchase (NDA planned 2026) [CLM-012149, CLM-012151, CLM-009076, CLM-009077]. Takeda exited cell therapy in October 2025, recognising a JPY 58.2bn impairment (JPY 58.0bn was the earlier expectation) [CLM-005025, CLM-009084]. Synthesis: [CLM-011058]. - Takeda's stated peak

docs.t: What the evidence shows Domain 2: Next-generation R&D (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: potential for six late-stage programs is USD 10-20bn [CLM-005041]; early pipeline depth beyond them is a gap (IVB-008) [CLM-005044]. Contrary evidence - Platform pipelines still suffer ordinary attrition [CLM-006047]; Lilly's DICE and AbbVie's Cerevel purchases ended in discontinuation or large impairment [CLM-009003, CLM-009054], so acquiring modalities is not safer than building them.

docs.t: Where proprietary advantage exists Domain 2: Next-generation R&D (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: - Disease biology depth (orexin) and clinical execution are proprietary and not purchasable quickly [CLM-005048, CLM-005042]. - Generative models and structure tools are converging on open or shared models (OpenFold3, Boltz, Chai), so the model itself is a weaker moat than proprietary assay and clinical data [CLM-006056]. - Partnering is better for new modalities where Takeda lacks platform scale; options reduce capital at risk compared with asset purchases [CLM-009099, CLM-009061] (INTERPRETATION) .

docs.t: What the evidence shows Domain 3: Robotics and autonomous science (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Deployed - High-throughput scripted automation is operational and commodity: Arctoris runs the former Lilly platform as a CRO service, with five biochemistry modules, a screening module, a BSL2 cell-biology module and 4 million compound storage, and expanded biophysics capacity ten-fold [CLM-006013, CLM-006016]. - Plant automation that operates is conventional: Lilly Lebanon Advanced Therapies opened 2026-05-06 with robotic dosing and sealing seen on a tour, no performance data [CLM-006002]. Announced or prototype - Lilly-NVIDIA co-innovation lab (up to USD 1bn over five years, jointly) targeting a continuous learning system linking agentic wet labs and dry labs: concept [CLM-000281]. LillyPod is operational compute with no reported result [CLM-006004, CLM-006007]. - Fast AI-to-wet-lab loops are vendor claims: Nabla three to four weeks design-to-test [CLM-006040]; BigHat pairs ML with a high-speed lab under an AbbVie deal [CLM-006035]. Robots and digital twins in Lilly plants are a vendor-blog capability claim, the audit calls the pilot tag generous [CLM-006006]. - Medicine Foundry (USD 4.5bn, opening late 2027) is concept [CLM-006000, CLM-006001]. Failures and exits - Lilly's Life Sciences Studio went to the CRO Arctoris in 2024; a reported USD 90m build cost conflicts on dates [CLM-006013, CLM-006014]. Zymergen sold to Ginkgo for about USD 300m, one-tenth of its IPO valuation, after USD 1.2bn cumulative net losses [CLM-006051]. Pattern: owned and venture-funded cloud lab or biofoundry models ended in divestment or distressed sale; the service model continues [CLM-006052, CLM-011063]. - J&J's Ottava (Auris) took a USD 0.9bn partial impairment in fiscal 2021 [CLM-009047]. This is device robotics, not lab robotics, but shows robotics capital risk. Takeda baseline - No public evidence of lab automation, continuous manufacturing or manufacturing robotics [CLM-005067]. Plasma network grew from 233 to 275 centers (FY2022-FY2024) and a USD 230m Los Angeles fractionation expansion adds up to 2 million litres per year [CLM-005063, CLM-005065].

docs.t: What the evidence shows Domain 4: Care models (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Deployed versus announced - Lilly: LillyDirect self-pay (Zepbound vials from August 2024 at USD 399/549, cut to USD 299/399/449 on 1 December 2025; KwikPen from USD 299); Lilly says over 1 million patients used LillyDirect in 2025 and one in three new branded weight-management starts was Zepbound self-pay vials (company-reported, footnotes unverified) [CLM-007000, CLM-007002, CLM-007044, CLM-007004]. - J&J: OTTAVA robot has De Novo authorisation (FDA decision 2026-07-21; announced 2026-07-22) and one announced installation, pilot maturity [CLM-000283, CLM-006029]; the A10 audit notes the release says the hospital "will be the first to install", so completion is not shown [CLM-000284]. Polyphonic is early access to select hospitals [CLM-006030]. - AbbVie Allē (over 6 million members, Jan 2024) is a loyalty scheme for aesthetics [CLM-007036]. Takeda Help at Hand: over 100,000 patients cumulative [CLM-007037]. - Convenience shifts: Entyvio subcutaneous pen approved in US, Europe, Japan and cited by Takeda as driving uptake; HYHUB needle-free transfer for Hyqvia received 510(k) clearance in July 2025 (clearance, not adoption) [CLM-007041, CLM-007042]. Counter-example: Spravato is restricted to certified sites under observation [CLM-007030]. - No adherence, persistence or time-to-therapy outcome was found for any company's programme; reported figures are enrolment or access counts [CLM-007039]. Synthesis: [CLM-011067]. Contrary evidence - Pear Therapeutics, a prescription digital therapeutics company, filed for Chapter 11 on 7 April 2023 after payers could deny payment; commentary says evidence was strong but reimbursement stalled [CLM-007045, CLM-007046]. Decentralised-trial disclosures were not usable in the Lilly or J&J 10-Ks [CLM-007048].
