docs.x: Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026. Options are labelled EVIDENCE BACKED or HYPOTHESIS; none is an endorsement. Evidence draws on A7's commercial models comparison.md and transfer to takeda.md. Problem addressed: protect and grow net revenue as payers, PBMs and price negotiation compress margins, and launch new brands on time. (INTERPRETATION) Design rule for this domain: separate decision support (AI that advises people) from automation that creates compliance risk (AI that generates, sends or targets promotional or patient-facing content without review). Evidence below is assigned to one or the other.

docs.t: What the evidence shows Domain 5: Commercial models (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Payer, PBM and policy dynamics (largest effect on commercial models) - CVS Caremark preferred Wegovy over Zepbound from 1 July 2025 (Lilly stock fell over 11% on the announcement) and restored Zepbound as an additional preferred option from 1 October 2026 [CLM-007011, CLM-007013]. - From 1 July 2026 CVS template formularies prefer interchangeable Stelara biosimilars [CLM-007015]. AbbVie reports USD 65.1bn of rebate and chargeback provisions in 2025 [CLM-007019]. AbbVie delayed Humira erosion by rebate-for-access contracting and a co-branded supply route [CLM-003085]. - Takeda: Entyvio was selected for Medicare price negotiation effective January 2028 [CLM-007026]. Synthesis: [CLM-011071]. Launch execution - Mounjaro USD 22,965m and Zepbound USD 13,542m in 2025, 56% of Lilly revenue, with lower realised prices [CLM-007031, CLM-007024]. Skyrizi USD 17,562m and Rinvoq USD 8,304m [CLM-007020]. Carvykti USD 1,887m was capacity-limited; Spravato USD 1,696m was site-limited [CLM-007029]. - Takeda: Entyvio JPY 958.0bn (21% of revenue) and QDENGA JPY 40.8bn; oveporexton and zasocitinib launches are pending [CLM-007027, CLM-005045, CLM-007033]. New-brand launch execution is POTENTIAL NEW CAPABILITY [CLM-005069, CLM-005074]. AI in commercial work: deployed versus announced - J&J reports AskJIA (sales assistant), Engagement.AI (provider insights, 14 countries) and a quality-control answer tool, with no usage or outcome data [CLM-006023, CLM-006021]. Maturity: operational per executive, self-reported. Contrary evidence - Cash-pay channels are limited by copay accumulators and anti-kickback rules; the self-pay share of Zepbound revenue is not in the 10-K [CLM-007010, CLM-007005]. Whether TrumpRx volumes are material is unknown [CLM-007009].

This is the thinnest domain in public evidence. Framing rule: this file does not treat workforce change as replacement of people by automation. Roles change when tasks are automated; the evidence below separates efficiency programmes, which Takeda describes in its own terms, from AI and automation effects, which are unquantified. docs.t: What the evidence shows Domain 7: People and operating model (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Competitors - J&J: nearly 900 generative-AI use cases were reviewed for risk, with 10-15% driving about 80% of value, and AI project ownership moved to departments to focus on high-value use cases (CIO interview relayed by a newsletter) [CLM-006018, CLM-006019]. 47,000 employees completed a required generative-AI course, which A10 treats as a training metric, not a deployment [CLM-006022]. Maturity: self-reported pilot to operational. - AbbVie: ARCH was built by fewer than ten full-time staff plus contractors, with a governance decision to open data to all R&D [CLM-006032, CLM-006034]. - Lilly: a chief AI officer organisation exists, with compute and data investments but no workforce data [CLM-006003, CLM-006007]. Takeda - 80% of the digital workforce was external when the transformation was designed, leading to large-scale insourcing through internal "digital factories" (executive interview via BCG, interested source) [CLM-005057]. Gabriele Ricci has been CDTO since February 2022 [CLM-005056]. - A March 2026 transformation targets over JPY 200bn gross annual savings by FY2028 through streamlining corporate functions, moving teams closer to patients and customers and process simplification; the cost series is JPY 150bn, 170bn then 160bn in successive company figures, and trade press reported about 4,500 role reductions (under 10% of roles) [CLM-005059, CLM-005078]. docs.t: Sequencing: does data infrastructure have to come first? (HYPOTHESIS argued from evidence) Strategic bets for Takeda, 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: Three positions are possible: (a) data infrastructure first, then automation; (b) a bounded lab-automation initiative that seeds its own data foundation; (c) both in parallel with a defined hand-off. The evidence supports (c) with a hard gate at stage 3. - Stages 1-2 of the automation ladder (assisted and scripted high-throughput work) are operational and commodity, and the continuing model is a service: Arctoris runs the former Lilly platform as a CRO and sells data generation to AI customers [CLM-006013] [CLM-006016] [CLM-011062]. A rented initiative (BET-09) therefore produces data without Takeda owning robots, and it can seed a structured assay dataset if a minimal schema is enforced from the first contract. This is a thin slice of BET-01, not the full layer. - Stage 3 and above (AI planning tied to wet labs) has no independent demonstration [CLM-011062]. Judging it needs a decision log and baselines (BET-01), because without them a vendor claim such as Nabla's three to four week loop cannot be tested against a conventional comparator [CLM-006040]. Zymergen paired automation and ML and sold at about one-tenth of its IPO-era valuation after USD 1.2bn of cumulative net losses [CLM-006051]. (INTERPRETATION) - The data layer is cheap relative to the cost of automating without it: AbbVie's ARCH was built by fewer than ten full-time staff plus contractors [CLM-006032]. This is one company's example, so the point is about order of magnitude, not a Takeda cost (see ASM-101). - Plasma operations are the exception: nomogram and process data already exist at site level [CLM-005060], so BET-02 can seed its own data foundation and does not wait for BET-01. Dependency chain (hard): BET-01 and BET-09 (H1 2027) - BET-07 benchmarking (needs both; RM-020 now depends on RM-015 and RM-018) - stage-3 pilot only if three triggers fire (independent Lilly-lab result, Nabla

Make Takeda's own trial, real-world, assay and plasma data reusable under one governed layer so that a small number of named decisions (target choice, trial design, supply planning) can be measured against a pre-agreed baseline. (RECOMMENDATION, conditional on IVB-001.) B. Future market change. Without an inventory of products, users and outcomes, spending cannot be linked to value (IVB-001). Whether Takeda's data estate is fragmented as AbbVie's was is unknown (HYPOTHESIS) [CLM-011055]. D. docs.t: 1. NVIDIA / CUDA (developer tools to hardware moat) Platform-strategy analogies for pharma (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Mechanism. NVIDIA announced CUDA in November 2006 [CLM-011000]. Its VP says CUDA succeeded because it changed C as little as possible, ran across GPU generations, "cost the company billions" and earned nothing for ten years [CLM-011003]. The 10-K says CUDA runs on all NVIDIA GPUs and over 7.5 million developers use it [CLM-011001]. Data Center revenue went from USD 47.5bn (FY2024) to USD 193.7bn (FY2026) [CLM-011002]. Mechanism summary [CLM-011024]. Evidence strength. T1 financials; the loss history is one interested executive's statement (T3 report of an interview) [CLM-011003]. Developer counts differ between the 10-K (7.5 million) and the company blog (11 million) [CLM-011000, CLM-011001]. Prediction for pharma. The durable asset is a data and model layer that others build on, since compute is purchasable; the closest pharma instance is Lilly TuneLab, operational with no outcome evidence [CLM-011025, CLM-000280, CLM-006007]. Where it breaks. Pharma has few buyers, each of which owns data; validation takes years through clinical trials; and NVIDIA's own 10-K lists customers' in-house capability and custom chips as a threat [CLM-011004, CLM-011026]. Contrary evidence. The risk factors above; also no pharma has reported developer adoption numbers for a model platform beyond Benchling's 1,300+ customer reach and a vendor blog's data-point counts [CLM-006008, CLM-009028]. Hypothesis for Takeda (HYPOTHESIS). Takeda gains more from joining a federated data layer than from building a proprietary platform [CLM-011027].
docs.h: 1. NVIDIA / CUDA (developer tools to hardware moat)

docs.t: 2. SpaceX reusable launch (iteration, vertical integration, infrastructure ownership) Platform-strategy analogies for pharma (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Mechanism. NASA documents give the cost outcome: Falcon 9 development about USD 390m (Falcon 9 USD 300m plus Falcon 1 USD 90m, verified by NASA) against NASA model estimates of USD 1.7-4.0bn [CLM-011005, CLM-011006]; a Falcon 9 plus Dragon ISS mission at about USD 140m (USD 23,300/kg versus USD 93,400/kg for the Shuttle), cost to the ISS down by a factor of four [CLM-011007]. The acquisition model was firm fixed price with cost risk on the supplier [CLM-011008]. Summary [CLM-011028]. Evidence strength. T1 NASA documents. The cause of the gap (iteration, vertical integration, fewer processes, reuse) is not isolated; NASA states it is difficult to determine why actual cost was so far below the model [CLM-011006]. Prediction for pharma. Gains in manufacturing and automation come from owning a whole loop and iterating hardware fast, and from buying outcomes at fixed price [CLM-011029]. Testable at plant scale: Takeda's Los Angeles plasma expansion (USD 230m) and Lilly's Medicine Foundry (USD 4.5bn, concept) [CLM-005065, CLM-006000]. Where it breaks. NASA records that each commercial cargo partner suffered catastrophic failures that the contract absorbed [CLM-011008]; in pharma a failed batch or trial can harm patients and GMP validation slows iteration; Takeda's own Hikari warning letter caused a supply shortage [CLM-011030, CLM-005020]. Hypothesis for Takeda (HYPOTHESIS). Contract plasma automation and digital upgrades fixed-price, outcome-linked, in one site before network roll-out [CLM-011031].

docs.t: 3. Google internal and external AI investment (optionality, outcomes, capital exposure, failures) Platform-strategy analogies for pharma (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Mechanism. Alphabet funds long-horizon research inside a profitable core (capex USD 91.4bn in 2025) and a separate Other Bets unit whose operating loss was USD 4.1bn (2023), USD 4.4bn (2024) and USD 7.5bn (2025, including a USD 2.1bn Waymo compensation charge) [CLM-011010, CLM-011009]. Documented outcome: AlphaFold2 predicted the structure of virtually all 200 million known proteins, used by over two million people in 190 countries, and shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry [CLM-011012]. Externally, Isomorphic Labs (a DeepMind spin-out) reportedly raised USD 600m (snippet) and signed Lilly (USD 45m upfront, up to USD 1.7bn) with no disclosed candidate [CLM-011014, CLM-006012]. Summary [CLM-011032]. Failures and capital exposure. Alphabet dissolved Google Health in August 2021 after about three years and roughly 500 staff (two snippets, pages not opened) [CLM-011013]; its 10-K says the life-sciences bets may not be successful or profitable [CLM-011011]. The Other Bets loss rose USD 3.1bn from 2024 to 2025 [CLM-011009]. Prediction for pharma. AI-for-biology advances arrive first as scientific tools and partnered spin-outs, not as drugs [CLM-011033]. Where it breaks. Alphabet funds from an advertising profit pool with no patent cliff; pharma funds R&D from products that lose exclusivity; Alphabet's capex alone exceeds any pharma AI disclosure by orders of magnitude [CLM-011034, CLM-011010]. Contrary evidence. Isomorphic raised outside capital, which suggests optionality cost can be shared [CLM-011014]. Hypothesis for Takeda (HYPOTHESIS). Copy only the capped-exposure rule: a ring-fenced AI and automation option budget with explicit stop criteria, consistent with Takeda's record of stops (soticlestat, cell therapy exit with a JPY 58.2bn impairment) [CLM-011035, CLM-005024, CLM-009084].

docs.t: 4. Regeneron VelociSuite (biotech platform factory) Platform-strategy analogies for pharma (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Mechanism. Regeneron replaced six megabases of mouse immunoglobulin loci with human loci (VelocImmune), and built VelociGene, VelociMouse, VelociMab, Veloci-Bi, VelociT and VelociHum for antibodies and bispecifics [CLM-011015]. The Regeneron Genetics Center has sequenced over 3 million samples with automation and cloud computing for target discovery [CLM-011016]. Summary [CLM-011036]. Evidence strength. T1 10-K; contribution to approved products is not quantified in the filing. Prediction for pharma. A proprietary discovery factory supplies molecules and targets across many programmes at lower marginal cost than buying assets (INTERPRETATION) . Where it breaks. EYLEA U.S. net sales fell 42% in 2025 and the company relies on Dupixent profit share from the Sanofi collaboration, so a platform does not protect individual product revenue [CLM-011017, CLM-011037]. Hypothesis for Takeda (HYPOTHESIS). Treat orexin science as a platform with a multi-asset plan, if a second differentiated asset is shown credible [CLM-011038, CLM-012149, CLM-005023].

docs.t: 5. TSMC and the foundry model (semiconductors) Platform-strategy analogies for pharma (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Mechanism. TSMC states it is a dedicated foundry, unveiled its Open Innovation Platform in 2008 with partners building design infrastructure, earned 74% of 2025 wafer revenue from 7 nm and below, spent NT$1.27 trillion on capex in 2025 and guides to US$52-56bn in 2026 [CLM-011018, CLM-011019]. Summary [CLM-011039]. Evidence strength. T1 20-F; the neutrality-toward-customers claim is TSMC's known positioning but was not located verbatim in the passages read (flagged in the claim). Prediction for pharma. A neutral capacity provider with a partner ecosystem wins when sponsors prefer not to build leading-edge capacity; pharma CDMOs are the nearest analogue (INTERPRETATION) . Where it breaks. Sponsors hold patents and guard process know-how and safety liability, and plasma carries donor-supply and regulatory limits that wafers do not [CLM-011040]. Hypothesis for Takeda (HYPOTHESIS, low confidence). Test a neutral-capacity or shared-analytics role in plasma if utilisation shows spare capacity [CLM-011041, CLM-005065].

docs.t: 6. AWS (cloud: internal capability productised) Platform-strategy analogies for pharma (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Mechanism. Amazon's 10-K describes AWS as a broad set of on-demand services to developers and enterprises [CLM-011020]. AWS had USD 128.7bn net sales and USD 45.6bn operating income in 2025, about 57% of Amazon's USD 80.0bn consolidated operating income (computed) [CLM-011020]. Summary [CLM-011042]. Prediction for pharma. The first pharma capability to be productised is one with standalone cost advantage and external demand; TuneLab is the nearest case [CLM-011043, CLM-009027]. Where it breaks. Pharma's would-be customers are competitors, and patient data is constrained by consent; consortia like AISB show rivals will cooperate only under federation [CLM-011044, CLM-006056]. Hypothesis for Takeda (HYPOTHESIS). Do not productise internal capabilities until a measured internal advantage exists; Takeda has none public [CLM-011045, CLM-006045].

docs.t: 7. Intuitive Surgical (industrial and medical robotics: installed base) Platform-strategy analogies for pharma (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Mechanism. About 11,106 da Vinci systems installed, about 3.15 million procedures in 2025, and recurring revenue (instruments, service, leases) of USD 8.47bn, 84% of revenue [CLM-011021]. Summary [CLM-011046]. Prediction for pharma. Value accrues to the owner of the installed base and per-use consumables, as with pens and devices tied to a drug (INTERPRETATION) . Where it breaks. J&J's robotics entry cost a USD 0.9bn Ottava impairment and OTTAVA has one announced installation; hospitals' capital cycles control adoption [CLM-011047, CLM-009047, CLM-006029]. Hypothesis for Takeda (HYPOTHESIS). Pull-through economics are cheaper to capture via drug-device combinations (Entyvio pen, HYHUB) than via robotics [CLM-011048, CLM-007041, CLM-007042].
docs.h: 7. Intuitive Surgical (industrial and medical robotics: installed base)

docs.t: 8. Roche-Flatiron (healthcare technology: data platform ownership) Platform-strategy analogies for pharma (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: Mechanism. Roche paid USD 1.9bn (closed 6 April 2018) and kept Flatiron a separate legal entity with segregated data; Flatiron then partnered with 14 of the top 15 oncology companies (2018 figures) [CLM-011022]. Flatiron markets regulatory use of its real-world data, shown here only as a vendor snippet [CLM-011023]. Summary [CLM-011049]. Prediction for pharma. A neutral data asset can serve competitors; ownership by one pharma works only if neutrality is protected (INTERPRETATION) . Where it breaks. Flatiron is oncology-specific and built in US community oncology; Takeda's core areas lack such a network, and Roche's realised value was not verified here [CLM-011050]. Hypothesis for Takeda (HYPOTHESIS). A neutral registry in a rare or plasma-treated disease could be a data moat, if built as a neutral entity [CLM-011051, CLM-005072]. ---

docs.t: Cross-analogy reading (INTERPRETATION) Platform-strategy analogies for pharma (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: - Two analogies (NVIDIA, AWS) depend on an installed developer or customer base that pharma lacks; two (SpaceX, TSMC) depend on capital-intensive operations where Takeda has plasma manufacturing; two (Intuitive, Regeneron) are about owning a repeatable engine; Google and Flatiron concern optionality and neutrality. - Takeda-specific hypotheses that survive the "where it breaks" test best are the ones tied to existing Takeda classes: PDT manufacturing (2), orexin (3) and drug-device combinations (1, 8). The rest are low-confidence. - No analogy is evidence that any of these moves works in pharma; each needs an internal test listed in the internal validation backlog.

docs.t: How to read the table Moat mechanisms taxonomy (A11b, wave 3)
docs.x: - A mechanism is a moat only if it is hard for a competitor to replicate and it changes an economic outcome; for data, learning and ecosystem moats the registry holds no independent outcome evidence for any competitor [CLM-006054 as corrected by A10: "wording stronger than sources support"]. - Infrastructure, IP and workflow moats are the best evidenced in competitor financials, but each carries a documented exposure: announced capacity is not operating capacity [CLM-006001]; patents expire (Entyvio) [CLM-005017]; PBM templates change [CLM-007015]. - Takeda's strongest evidenced moats sit in mechanisms 3 (orexin science, in-house), 4 (plasma network) and 7 (late-stage development execution) [CLM-005048, CLM-005063, CLM-005042]. Its weakest evidenced are 1, 2 and 6, where no outcomes are public [CLM-005080].

docs.t: Reading the table (INTERPRETATION) Scenarios 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: - SCN-3 (pricing, regulatory and biosimilar pressure): under the published ratings no bet is robust. BET-04 is needed but its value holds only as delay: the January 2028 Medicare price is statutory and PBM private-label biosimilars route around contracts [CLM-007026] [CLM-007015]. BET-11 is fragile because SC moves patients into the pharmacy benefit. - SCN-2 (AI incremental) is the base case for AI spending: no independent outcome exists for any AI platform [CLM-011052]. BET-07 is fragile there; its v2 size is small and its tranches are gated. - SCN-5 (combined downside): about half of the v2 constrained envelope (50%) sits in bets the council rates fragile (table above); BET-03 and BET-05 stay funded as floors because they act inside or after the Entyvio window and nothing else replaces them. - Early entry (S-A): BET-05 is the only replacement in time; BET-03 and BET-06 payoff misses the window; the playbook is moved to 2028 H1 (RM-026) and the bridge is BET-18 within the leverage headroom (ASM-119). - Option value: BET-10 (rejected) only pays off if SCN-1 shows demonstrated autonomy; the operational trigger set keeps that option at zero capital [CLM-011066].

docs.t: Timing: what needs an early start and what can wait Scenarios 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: Early start (capability building takes years or dates are fixed): - BET-04 Entyvio franchise defence: payer contracting, evidence and lifecycle: Fixed external dates: benefit-channel gate 2027 H1, January 2028 negotiation [CLM-007026], biosimilar reviews and possible 2028-2029 entry [CLM-014051], 2032 patents [CLM-005017]. - BET-02 Plasma process-intelligence and fixed-price automation programme: Baseline, demand-versus-capacity test and plasma-peer benchmark take 2-3 years; the network decision should precede capacity commitments [CLM-005065]. - BET-03 Orexin science as a multi-asset discovery platform: Discovery to a second asset takes many years (INTERPRETATION); delay moves refill beyond 2035. - BET-01 Governed cross-franchise R&D data and decision layer: Thin slice must exist before stage-3 automation or AI-design benchmarking. - BET-17 AI use-case measurement, decision support and reskilling: Baselines must exist before any value claim; cheap. - BET-05 Zasocitinib breadth and immunology successor evidence: Regulatory dates drive timing [CLM-005035] [CLM-005037]. - BET-06 Option-based external innovation engine incl. new-modality options: Option pipeline needs 5-10 years to show approvals [CLM-009097]. - BET-11 Drug-device and home/SC administration platform: Device development cycles and approvals [CLM-007042]. - BET-12 Launch-pathway partnerships and patient-services outcome measurement: Attach to the oveporexton launch (approved 2026-08-05 [CLM-005029]); a 2027 H2 pilot is late, so the start moves to 2027 H1. Can be postponed (or is triggered): - BET-13 Neutral rare-disease or plasma real-world data registry: Needs BET-12 data; revisit 2029. - BET-10 Owned autonomous discovery lab (stage 4-5): Triggers not yet fired. - BET-14 TuneLab-style productised external model platform: No measured advantage. - BET-07 Milestone-gated AI-design partnerships (Nabla, Iambic and successors): Scale only after first-in-human data; existing alliances continue. - BET-09 Rented automated data generation (CRO and cloud labs) with ladder triggers: Stage-3 pilot waits on triggers; stage 1-2 can start now. - BET-08 Federated data consortium participation: Cheap; can start any time but value rests on BET-01. - BET-18 Phase

docs.t: Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6) Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: Version v2 (A11c-bis, 2026-11-21): numbers and decisions follow the Director's decision record. See 'Changes from v1' at the end. Research cutoff 2026-11-21. This narrative summarises the proposals in strategic bets.md, capital allocation.md, stage gates.md, scenarios 2027 2040.md, loe resilience strategy.md and roadmap 2027 2040.md. It uses public evidence only. Takeda's budget and internal data are unknown, so every figure that is not a registry claim is an ASSUMPTION with an id. FACT, INTERPRETATION, HYPOTHESIS, SCENARIO and RECOMMENDATION are kept apart.
docs.h: Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)

docs.t: 1. What is changing Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: (FACT) Entyvio, 21% of FY2025 revenue (JPY 958.0bn), loses regulatory exclusivity in the latter half of the decade, has patents expiring in 2032, faces two biosimilar BLAs under FDA review and enters Medicare negotiation in January 2028 [CLM-005009] [CLM-005017] [CLM-014051] [CLM-007026]. v2 widens the entry-year range to 2028-2032 (central case 2031 unchanged) and adds an early-entry stress case (ASM-025, ASM-038). PBM template formularies now decide biosimilar outcomes [CLM-007015]. AI and automation are being built at scale by competitors, but no company in the set shows an independent outcome [CLM-011052].

docs.t: 2. Who is winning, and why Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: (FACT) Lilly's revenue rose from USD 28.3bn to USD 65.2bn between FY2021 and FY2025 because tirzepatide reached 56.0% of sales, backed by capacity spending [CLM-000133] [CLM-001003] [CLM-000172]. AbbVie replaced Humira with Skyrizi and Rinvoq because the successors were already marketed across Humira's indications [CLM-003014] [CLM-003084]. J&J absorbed Stelara with a diversified base; its largest brand is 15.2% of revenue [CLM-002073]. (INTERPRETATION) Winning here means pre-built successors, capacity and diversification. It does not yet mean AI: Lilly's advantage in growth is a launched molecule in a supply-short category, and realised prices already fell 15% in Q3 2026 [CLM-014003]. The ranking of 'new-molecule revenue share' is not used because the audit marks it invalid as a productivity comparison.

docs.t: 3. What is defensible Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: (INTERPRETATION) Compute and third-party models are purchasable; proprietary data, capacity and clinical execution are not [CLM-006055] [CLM-011085]. Competitor data, learning and ecosystem moats have no independent outcome evidence; infrastructure, IP and workflow moats are the best evidenced but each is removable (announced capacity is not operating capacity, patents expire, PBM templates change) [CLM-006054] [CLM-006001] [CLM-007015].

docs.t: 4. What Takeda already has Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: (FACT) A plasma network of 270+ centres with adaptive nomograms and a USD 230m fractionation expansion; in-house orexin science that produced an approval on 2026-08-05; late-stage execution on schedule (three approvals or filings); stop discipline (soticlestat, cell therapy exit with a JPY 58.2bn impairment); and deal flow with Nimbus, Protagonist and Innovent [CLM-005060] [CLM-005065] [CLM-005048] [CLM-012149] [CLM-005042] [CLM-005024] [CLM-005025] [CLM-009076] [CLM-009078]. The enterprise data platform exists but outcomes are unproven; lab automation, AI-enabled discovery and patient services are public-evidence gaps, not proven absences [CLM-005058] [CLM-005067] [CLM-005049] [CLM-005072] [CLM-005080].

docs.t: 5. Where the opportunity is Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: (RECOMMENDATION) In order of evidence strength: (1) defend and extend the dated Entyvio exposure (BET-04, BET-11); (2) back the replacement set already in hand (BET-05) and hold a funded, contingent mid-size licensing channel for the 2031-2034 gap (BET-18); (3) test whether plasma process data (BET-02, EXPERIMENT: baseline and shadow-mode first, because no plasma peer is benchmarked) and orexin biology (BET-03, at the constrained size with a Phase 1 gate) can become compounding assets; (4) hold cheap options on AI and new modalities and let data decide (BET-06, BET-07, BET-08, BET-09); (5) build the measurement discipline that makes every AI claim testable (BET-01, BET-17, BET-12).

docs.t: 6. What to build, what to partner, what to reject Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: BUILD: governed data and decision layer on the existing platform (BET-01), orexin platform at USD 300m (BET-03), Entyvio defence with a benefit-channel gate (BET-04), devices, baseline first (BET-11). INVEST: zasocitinib breadth (BET-05). PARTNER: scorecard-first options and licences (BET-06), milestone-gated AI design (BET-07), federated consortia (BET-08), rented automation (BET-09), Phase 2/3 licensing channel, contingent (BET-18, new). EXPERIMENT: plasma process intelligence, baseline and shadow-mode (BET-02, was BUILD), launch pathways at USD 50m (BET-12), AI measurement and decision support (BET-17, owner independent of the CFO). DEFER: neutral registry (BET-13, no carry). REJECT: owned autonomous lab (BET-10, with an operational trigger set), TuneLab-style platform (BET-14), a USD 5bn+ purchase (BET-15, was DEFER), U.S. cash-pay channel (BET-16). Sequencing: the data standard and rented automation start together in H1 2027; stage-3 closed-loop work waits for the full data layer and three observable triggers [CLM-011066].

docs.t: 7. What to invest Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: (ASSUMPTION) Three portfolios of incremental capital over 2027-2040: capital-constrained USD 1,130m (v1 1,590m), balanced USD 1,920m committed at gates (v1 2,950m), ambitious USD 3,155m (v1 4,975m) (ASM-003, ASM-002, ASM-004), roughly 1.8%, 3.0% and 5.0% of fourteen years of flat R&D at ASM-001. Balanced is the proposed starting point: the H1 2027-29 tranche is USD 595m, of which USD 465m is core (BET-01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 08, 09, 11, 17) and USD 130m (BET-06, 07, 12) is released only on triggers. About USD 1,030m of contingent headroom is reserved for the BET-18 licensing channel (ASM-118); it is not a saving and is released only if the leverage test passes (ASM-033, ASM-119, IVB-012). A USD 5bn+ purchase is rejected as framed.

docs.t: 8. How to execute Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: Stage gates with stop and expansion criteria and named roles: discovery, feasibility, prototype, pilot, scale, value review. The first decision points are the Entyvio benefit-channel gate (2027 H1), the plasma-peer and additionality gates (2027 H2), the January 2028 Entyvio posture with the biosimilar playbook live in 2028 H1, and the Nabla and Iambic go/no-go (2028 H2). A portfolio review each year compares scenario signals (SCN-1 to SCN-5) and reallocates between the three portfolios.

docs.t: 9. How to measure Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)

docs.t: 10. Reader paragraphs Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: CEO. The decision is whether to treat Entyvio's cliff as a dated defence plus a refill problem, or as a reason to chase a platform story. The evidence supports the first. The proposal funds the dated defence and the replacement set, keeps AI and new modalities as capped options with stop rules, and explicitly rejects four expensive alternatives (owned autonomous lab, external model platform, U.S. cash-pay, and a USD 5bn+ purchase that fails the 3.0x leverage ceiling by arithmetic). For the owned lab the competitor record is weaker than it looks: Lilly's reason for selling is undisclosed and the NVIDIA joint lab reads as re-platforming [CLM-006017] [CLM-000281]; Zymergen failed on a different model [CLM-006051]; U.S. cash-pay has poor structural fit [CLM-007052]. Execution load is high: a new CEO since 24 June 2026, a restructuring and three launches within twelve months [CLM-005073] [CLM-005074]. CFO. Capital is proposed as ranges in three envelopes that depend on leverage (2.6x at March 2026) and Amitiza cash (JPY 403.5bn provision, timing unknown) [CLM-005005] [CLM-005014]. Contingent payments in AI and option deals (over USD 1bn on single deals) cost nothing without data and are not in the envelope [CLM-006039] [CLM-006041]. No NPV is reported: it would require internal forecasts and probabilities (IVB-004, IVB-005, IVB-014). The capital-constrained portfolio keeps the dated defences and drops AI-scale and option spend first; the registry carries no capital in any portfolio. Mid-size licences (BET-18) are released only if leverage stays at or below ASM-033 after Amitiza clarity and a write-down test passes, because AbbVie wrote off 54% of Cerevel's net price [CLM-009054]; council arithmetic puts a USD 5bn purchase at about 3.1x and about 3.4x with Amitiza (ASM-119). R&D. Refill after 2030 depends on early depth that is not public (IVB-008). The proposal funds a second orexin-class asset as discovery spend

docs.t: 10. Reader paragraphs Executive strategy narrative: Takeda 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)
docs.x: at the constrained size with a Phase 1 gate and an additionality test, scorecard-first option access to one or two adjacent modalities, and AI-design partnerships gated on first-in-human data and comparator benchmarks [CLM-011038] [CLM-011061] [CLM-006039]. Gate CNS assets on Phase 2 quality: neuroscience was the common failure site across three companies [CLM-003054] [CLM-002039] [CLM-012120]. Rent wet-lab automation rather than own it; the owned-lab failures are weaker evidence than a pattern [CLM-006013] [CLM-011065]. CTO / Chief Digital and Technology Officer. Extend the existing agent platform with governance, a decision log and baselines; do not build a competing platform [CLM-005058]. The model layer converges on shared models, so the moat is Takeda's own decision-linked data [CLM-006056] [CLM-006055]. Join federated tasks where measured gains exist [CLM-006043]. Document model credibility against the January 2025 FDA draft framework [CLM-006046]. Sequence: data standard and rented automation together; closed-loop work only after the full layer and three triggers. Commercial. Settle the benefit-channel split in 2027 H1, then build payer-contracting and formulary-defence depth for Entyvio before January 2028 and the biosimilar window (possibly as early as 2028); the aim is to delay and measure erosion, since Humira's contracting delayed but did not prevent it [CLM-003007] [CLM-003002]. Extend SC and home administration baseline-first, and settle with the Entyvio team whether moving patients into the pharmacy benefit helps or hurts after entry, which is unproven [CLM-007041] [CLM-007042] [CLM-007053] [CLM-007015]. Attach a USD 50m-capped launch-pathway pilot to oveporexton from 2027 H1, with a named leader, before redesigning patient programmes, since AbbVie's redesign was reversed within months [CLM-003033]. Do not copy a U.S. cash-pay channel [CLM-007052]. Keep AI in field and medical teams advisory only; no automated promotional content.

docs.x: Status amendment rule. A claim's statement is immutable. The Director may amend status , maturity , basis , event date , single interested source , implications and add a correction ONLY when (a) an independent auditor proposed it in a conflicts proposed .jsonl file, (b) the change is applied by a script ( scripts/apply audit .py ) that appends an audit history entry to the record and a line to conflicts.jsonl . Contradictory new evidence still goes in as a new claim linked through conflicts.jsonl . Multi-agent operation. Shard-isolated specialist agents (ID ranges in agent protocols.md ), single-writer merge ( scripts/merge shards.py ), one independent audit round per wave, fresh-context synthesis and council. Subagent default tool-call cap is 100 — briefs must raise it and require save-as-you-go. No derived numbers in prose. Durations, counts and percentages computed by an author must either be registered as a claim or be labelled INTERPRETATION with the inputs' claim IDs (three such errors were caught by audit round 2). Announcement ≠ regulator date. Approval dates are taken from FDA/EMA records; company announcement dates are recorded separately (three corrections in round 2).

docs.t: 4. Research conduct AGENT PROTOCOLS — how specialist agents work in MEDICINE
docs.x: - Source hierarchy T1 T2 T3 T4; T5 never as fact. Press release = announcement happened, not value realized. - Search by: company+domain, molecule/target, platform+partner, executive name, period, NCT number, deal identifier, DOI, and explicitly for failure / delay / discontinued / criticism / lawsuit . - Open the primary document. Quote the passage. Record the locator. - For every "capability" claim, ask: problem, what was built/bought, enablers (data/talent/IP/infra/partners), pilot vs production, operational change, measurable outcome, cost (if disclosed), defensibility. - Seek contrary evidence for each major finding; record it in contrary evidence . - Rate-limit yourself ( = 1 s between requests to one host). docs.t: Rules Source quality rules
docs.x: 1. Inspect before citing. Store a verbatim passage (<= 600 chars) and locator. 2. One original = one source. Syndicated repeats of a press release do not add independence. 3. Interested-party claims are flagged. "Company says X improved Y%" is a FACT about the statement, INTERPRETATION about the outcome unless independently corroborated. 4. Numbers carry period, currency, accounting basis (GAAP/non-GAAP/IFRS; continuing vs total operations). J&J pre/post-Kenvue (Aug 2023) and AbbVie post-Allergan (May 2020) are not comparable without adjustment. 5. Dates: distinguish event date, publication date, access date. 6. Access: retrieved (opened), api json (machine-read), metadata only (known to exist, not opened), paywalled , blocked (403/robot), unavailable (404/down). Never bypass paywalls/logins; respect robots and rate limits ( = 1 s/host). 7. Preserve conflicts in conflicts.jsonl with both source IDs and a resolution note (or unresolved ). 8. Lawful storage: full copies only for public records (SEC, FDA, CT.gov, government). Otherwise metadata + short excerpt + own notes. 9. Causality: two events in sequence are not cause and effect. Mark causal: asserted by company corroborated unknown . 10. Failure search is mandatory: for every company and domain, run at least one query for discontinued/failed/delayed/recall/lawsuit/criticism.

docs.x: - The filesystem is the system of record. Save after every ~5 sources. Never end with unsaved findings. - Every source you cite must have been OPENED by you (web fetch, the CLI fetch , or a file on disk). access status: retrieved REQUIRES a verbatim inspected passage (≤600 chars) you actually saw. If you only saw a search snippet, register it as metadata only and say so in notes . - No invented URLs, page numbers, quotes, numbers, dates. Put your reading in implication , never in statement . - Press release = announcement happened ≠ value realized. docs.t: Part 1 — Seven transformation domains (one file each under strategy/future of pharma/ ) A11b — Module 1: How Takeda can help shape the future of pharma (wave 3) + platform analogies
docs.x: domain1 data advantage.md , domain2 next gen rd.md , domain3 robotics autonomous science.md , domain4 care models.md , domain5 commercial models.md , domain6 partnerships.md , domain7 people operating model.md . For each domain: (a) what the evidence shows competitors have actually deployed vs announced (claim IDs, maturity); (b) the scientific/operational problem it addresses; (c) where proprietary capability creates advantage vs where open standards/partnering is better; (d) Takeda fit — therapeutic mix (GI, rare, PDT, neuroscience, oncology, vaccines), economics, evidence requirements — tied to the baseline class; (e) credible options (not endorsements) with what would have to be true; (f) measurable success criteria; (g) risks incl. compliance/safety (Domain 5: separate decision support from automation that creates compliance risk; Domain 7: do not frame workforce change as replacement by automation). docs.t: 4. Ask — grounded Q&A without heavy LLMs A13 (wave 3b) — Turn the application into the final "go-to" content hub: Takeda white/red design, full report reader, pillar architecture, grounded Q&A, single-file export
docs.x: - Pipeline builds qa index.json : passages = every claim (statement + implication + entities + company + domains + ids), every report section (heading + ~300-word chunk, path, pillar) and every source title. In the browser implement BM25 (own ~80-line TS or minisearch ) with field boosts; stemming light (lowercase, strip plurals). - Retrieval-only answer (default, always works, zero cost): top 8–12 passages → "Grounded answer" composed as cited bullets (claim statement + kind badge + company + source link), grouped by company/domain, with a "What the evidence base does not say" line when fewer than 3 strong matches, and the golden questions as suggestions. The negative test must hold: a question with no evidence returns "no evidence in the corpus", never an invented answer. - Optional "Synthesize with an open-source LLM" toggle: provider A = local Ollama ( http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/chat , model default qwen2.5:3b , OpenAI-compatible path also fine), provider B = any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (base URL + key entered by the user, stored only in localStorage; e.g. Groq/HF free tiers). Status pill checks /api/tags . Strict grounding prompt: "Answer only from the numbered evidence passages; cite [CLM-…]; if the passages do not answer, say so"; temperature 0; stream tokens; show the retrieved passages beneath the answer; label "LLM synthesis — verify against the cited claims". Fallback to retrieval-only when unreachable, with one-line setup instructions ( brew install ollama && ollama pull qwen2.5:3b && ollama serve ). The Director is installing Ollama in parallel; do not install anything yourself. Never send anything except the question and retrieved passages.

docs.t: Deliverables A11c — Module 2: Takeda's long-horizon strategic bets, capital allocation, stage gates, scenarios, roadmap (wave 4)
docs.x: 1. investment theses/strategic bets.md — ≥12 candidate platforms (the master prompt's 12 plus any you derive from the evidence; do NOT auto-endorse). For EVERY candidate the full template A–M: thesis; future market change; problem; evidence (claim IDs from competitor research + science); moat mechanism (which of data/learning/IP/infrastructure/workflow/network/regulatory/ecosystem, and why it compounds); practical architecture (build/buy/license/partner); investment (initial/follow-on/scaled, scenario-based with stated assumptions — Takeda's budget is NOT known: use ranges anchored to disclosed comparables, e.g., Lilly–NVIDIA up to USD 1bn/5y [CLM-000281], Nimbus USD 4bn [see A5/A9 claims], Takeda R&D JPY 675.9bn FY2025 [A5 claims], and label every number ASSUMPTION with an ASM- id); time to value; measurable outcomes; risks (scientific, regulatory, execution, data, competition, capital, adoption); strategic options (expand/redirect/partner/divest/stop); decision BUILD/PARTNER/INVEST/ACQUIRE/EXPERIMENT/DEFER/REJECT; evidence & confidence (known / assumed / needs Takeda internal validation → IVB ids). Baseline class for each (from capability baseline.md). Sequencing dependencies explicit (e.g., is data infrastructure a prerequisite to automated science, or can a bounded lab-automation initiative seed its own data foundation? argue from evidence). 2. financial cases/capital allocation.md — horizons H1 2027–29 / H2 2030–34 / H3 2035–40; three portfolios (capital-constrained, balanced, ambitious) with allocation % by horizon and theme (core capability / adjacent / long-horizon bets / external innovation) as proposals with assumptions; evaluation per bet (risk-adjusted NPV only where meaningful — otherwise say why not; expected value & downside; real-option value qualitatively; PTS; commercial probability; time to payoff; capability reuse; differentiation; capital efficiency; regulatory feasibility; execution complexity; synergy with Takeda assets; follow-on options). No false precision: ranges, not point estimates; every input traceable to a claim or an ASM- . 3. financial cases/stage gates.md — per material bet: discovery → feasibility → prototype/initial evidence → controlled pilot → scale decision → ongoing value review; at each gate capital at risk, evidence required, commercial milestone, stop criteria,

docs.t: Substantive findings A10 audit: wave-1 claim re-inspection (Task 1)
docs.x: 1. NUMBER MISMATCH / mislabel, CLM-003042 (and its sources CLM-000066..000070, CLM-000128..000132). "Non-current" long-term debt is in fact total long-term debt including the current portion for AbbVie (XBRL tag LongTermDebt ) and J&J. AbbVie FY2025: 64,503 is "Long-term debt, including current portion" (current 6,000; long-term 58,503 in the contractual-obligations table) and the balance-sheet non-current line is 58,941 (FY2024 60,340; FY2023 52,194; FY2022 59,135; FY2021 64,189). J&J FY2025: 41,438 is the debt-note subtotal; "Total long-term debt" after the current portion of 2,000 is 39,438 (FY2024 32,400 vs 30,651). Lilly ( LongTermDebtNoncurrent ) is correct. 20 claims carry the wrong label. 2. NOT FOUND IN SOURCE, CLM-006017. The claim about a "Lilly-Strateos remote robotic laboratory (public launch about 2020)" cites two BiopharmaTrend articles that never mention Strateos. They describe the Lilly Life Sciences Studio (established 2017, USD 90m). The 2020 date and the Strateos link are unsupported by the cited pages. 3. Maturity labels not justified by the evidence. CLM-006026 (VELYS) is tagged SCALED although the 10-K gives no system or procedure counts; CLM-006022 (course completions) is tagged SCALED; CLM-006047, -006049, -006051 are tagged DEMONSTRATED OUTCOME but describe failures at Recursion, Exscientia/BenevolentAI and Zymergen, not AI applications at the four companies. CLM-006020 (J&J 2.6x enrollment) is tagged OPERATIONAL on a single self-reported interview statement. Maturity values are also upper-case, whereas the protocol enumerates lower-case. 4. Registry understates retrievability. SRC-000034 (J&J OTTAVA release), SRC-009022 (CDD TuneLab blog) and SRC-009017 (BioPharma Dive) are registered metadata only but returned full pages in this audit. The OTTAVA page says Memorial Hermann "will be the first hospital to install" the system (future tense); CLM-000284 and the J&J master report ("first install 2026-11-19") present the installation as completed. The 19-Nov-2026 date does not appear in the page text I read. 5. Partly unreachable component. CLM-005025: the JPY 58.0bn cell-therapy

docs.t: What this means for use A10-bis Task 2: citation consistency of the synthesis layer
docs.x: Citation hygiene is good: no invented IDs, no unsupported company-level number found in the policy, domain and analogy layers beyond items 1, 2, 4, 8, 11 and 14. The items most likely to mislead a reader are 1 (debt), 8 (11 months), 11 (EVIDENCE BACKED on vendor evidence) and 14 (dates in the partnership domain).

docs.t: A10-bis Task 1: re-inspection of wave 2/3 shards A10-bis Task 1: re-inspection of wave 2/3 shards
docs.x: Date 2026-11-21. Auditor A10-bis. Method: every verdict below comes from a source I opened myself in this session (openFDA and ClinicalTrials.gov APIs queried live, FDA De Novo database, CMS fact-sheet PDFs, SEC filings on disk and from EDGAR, NASA NTRS PDFs, Nobel, Roche and company releases). Codes: PASS / LOCATOR FIX / NUMBER MISMATCH / PERIOD MISMATCH / NOT FOUND / UNREACHABLE. UNREACHABLE means I could not open the source (HTTP 403 or block page), not that the claim is wrong. Sample size: 92 claim verdicts in the stratified sample (A12 20, A8 13, A7 14, A14 22, A11 19, plus 4 cross-shard findings), plus a full sweep of 46 A12 FDA approval-date claims (46 of 46 match openFDA) and 43 of 43 A12 ClinicalTrials.gov status claims (all match the live record). Full machine-readable list: audit wave2 reinspection.jsonl (165 records).

docs.t: Result in one paragraph A10-bis Task 1: re-inspection of wave 2/3 shards
docs.x: No wrong number was found in A12, A8, A7, A14 or A11 FACT claims. The defects found are (1) date-label errors where a company announcement date is stored as the FDA action date (CLM-003063 Juvmo 09-28 vs FDA 09-25; CLM-000283 and CLM-006029 OTTAVA De Novo 07-22 vs FDA 07-21), (2) seven claims I could not re-open because investor.lilly.com, jnj.com and computerweekly.com return 403, so those rest on the stored passage only, (3) CLM-007002 whose stored passage does not contain half of the prices the statement lists, (4) CLM-012109 bermekimab 0.6bn which is a subsequent-event estimate later booked at 0.8bn, and (5) CLM-012137 whose registry date (2026) postdates the 2023 withdrawal it is paired with.

docs.t: 5. Maturity tags A10-bis Task 3: kind and status discipline on the new shards
docs.x: Missing: none on A14 or A7 FACT claims that concern AI or robotics. A11 INTERPRETATION, HYPOTHESIS and RECOMMENDATION claims about AI and automation (CLM-011025, 011029, 011031, 011033, 011035, 011043, 011045, 011047, 011048, 011053, 011060, 011064..011066, 011071, 011074, 011076, 011080..011083, 011085, 011087..011090, 011092..011095, 011097, 011098) have no maturity tag. They are claims about options, not capabilities, so propose a tag of the maturity of the cited competitor evidence (for example CLM-011065 rests on the divested Arctoris model, OPERATIONAL but commodity; CLM-011060 on PROTOTYPE partnerships). Tags that do not fit the evidence: - CLM-014073 DEMONSTRATED OUTCOME: a former CEO's interview claim of about 30% shorter narcolepsy trial development, no baseline or method, T3, PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. It contradicts the master report's statement that no AI initiative shows a demonstrated outcome. Retag PILOT and flag single interested source (conflict record filed). - CLM-014043 SCALED: 63.4% of staff "actively using" generative AI and 30.9% taking a course. Usage and training counts are adoption metrics; A10 round 1 made the same retag for J&J course completions. Propose OPERATIONAL. - CLM-014030 PROTOTYPE on the Capstan acquisition (an asset-acquisition accounting claim). Not an AI or robotics capability; use not applicable. - CLM-014025 OPERATIONAL on the MONARCH QUEST 3 clearance: the claim is PARTIALLY SUPPORTED and the "AI-powered" features are company marketing; the openFDA record only shows substantial equivalence for the platform. Propose PILOT for the AI feature, OPERATIONAL only for the device. - CLM-014022, CLM-014023, CLM-014024 are tagged PILOT for OTTAVA (authorised, one announced early-access installation). Reasonable and consistent with the master text.

docs.t: 6. A11 strategy claims A10-bis Task 3: kind and status discipline on the new shards
docs.x: Counts: 52 INTERPRETATION, 17 HYPOTHESIS, 7 RECOMMENDATION, 24 FACT. Status: 62 PARTIALLY SUPPORTED, 17 NEEDS MORE RESEARCH, 21 SUPPORTED. - EVIDENCE BACKED recommendations are PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. CLM-011054, 011060, 011065, 011068, 011069, 011072 and 011073 carry the label EVIDENCE BACKED in their text and in the domain tables while the registry status is PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. One label should win. Propose relabelling them "SUPPORTED BY ANALOGY: based on competitor evidence, not tested on Takeda", or keeping EVIDENCE BACKED and upgrading the status after the weak step is repaired. The weakest: CLM-011054 (pooled models beat Takeda-only models; the evidence is a vendor-organised consortium result against public models, not peer reviewed), CLM-011072 (relies on T4 Drug Channels and a CVS release for Entyvio biosimilar risk; Entyvio biosimilars have FDA review dates only from a trade snippet, CLM-014051), CLM-011073 (a "do not" recommendation resting on CRS description of copay rules and an inference about fit). - HYPOTHESIS that reads as a recommendation. CLM-011045 ("Takeda should not attempt to productise ...") and CLM-011066 ("Takeda should set explicit triggers ...") use directive wording. Retype as RECOMMENDATION with its own evidence label or reword as "Takeda could". - FACT claims in A11. I re-opened 19 of the 24 against primary text (NVIDIA, Alphabet, Regeneron, TSMC, Amazon and Intuitive 10-K or 20-F; NASA documents; Nobel; Roche). All numbers match. CLM-011003 (CUDA quotes) could not be re-opened (Computer Weekly 403) and rests on one interested speaker via T3; it is correctly flagged. docs.x: Answer from the registry. - OTTAVA table-integrated soft-tissue robot: IDE approval announced 2024-11-12 [CLM-002048]; De Novo submission announced 2026-01-07 [CLM-002049]; De Novo authorization 2026-07-22 [CLM-000283]; first hospital (Memorial Hermann-TMC) announced 2026-11-19 [CLM-000284]; FY2021 partial IPR&D impairment of USD 0.9bn on delays [CLM-009047]. - MONARCH bronchoscopy: 510(k) for QUEST 3 software announced 2026-08-17 [CLM-006027]; TARGET study 679 patients, 98.7% lesion reach, 83.2% diagnostic yield (company-sponsored, single arm) [CLM-002067]. - VELYS: Spine 510(k) announced 2024-08-02 [CLM-002066]; Knee growth "pull through" in the 10-K with no counts [CLM-006026]. - Polyphonic digital ecosystem in early access; Abu Dhabi programme [CLM-006030, CLM-006031]. - Capital deployment: Abiomed (USD 17.1bn net; FY2025 sales 1,751m) [CLM-002009, CLM-002027], Shockwave (FY2025 sales 1,146m) [CLM-002011], Orthopaedics separation as DePuy Synthes announced October 2025 [CLM-002030, CLM-002037]. - Safety/regulatory friction: FDA Class I recall classification of the Varipulse correction [CLM-002045] and of Impella pumps (66,390 units, 49 deaths recorded) [CLM-002046]. - Regulator-verified status as stated: "only OTTAVA ... regulator-verified milestone" [CLM-000286, CLM-006054]. Audit. - Only two J&J MedTech claims rest on FDA records (T1, regulatory record ): the Varipulse recall [CLM-002045] and the Impella recall [CLM-002046]. The De Novo, 510(k) and IDE statements [CLM-000283, -006027, -002066, -002048] are sourced to J&J press releases (T2). - A10 independent check: openFDA 510(k) database lists MONARCH Platform K260382 (decision 2026-07-25) and K243219 (2025-01-23), and VELYS Robotic-Assisted Solution K260480 (2026-06-25), K240211 (2024-06-05). I found no "VELYS Spine" device name by the name search tried. openFDA has no De Novo endpoint, so the OTTAVA De Novo is still UNVERIFIED against a regulator record. - "Regulator-verified" in CLM-000286 and CLM-006054 is therefore an overstatement of the sourcing, although the underlying event is plausible and the MONARCH clearance is now verified. - CLM-000284: the release says the hospital "will be the first to install"; the answer must not say a

U.S. Humira revenue 17,330 / 18,619 / 12,160 / 7,142 / 3,062 (USD m, 2021-25) [CLM-003001]; global 20,694 / 21,237 / 14,404 / 8,993 / 4,540, i.e. 2025 is 21% of the 2022 peak [CLM-003002]. Total revenue 58,054 (2022), 54,318 (2023, -6.4%), 56,334 (2024), 61,160 (2025, +8.6%) [CLM-003015]. Nine biosimilars launched in 2023 [CLM-003006]; Humira kept at least 97% of adalimumab volume through March 2024 [CLM-003007]; CVS Caremark exclusion from April 2024 and co-branded Cordavis supply [CLM-003008, CLM-003009]; Skyrizi and Rinvoq gained new indications 2022-2025 [CLM-003016]; 2027 target above USD 31bn [CLM-003022]. docs.t: Q4. Which reported AI applications at any of the four companies have demonstrated scientific or operational impact? A10: controlled questions, wave 1 (Task 5)
docs.x: Answer the corpus supports: none is independently demonstrated. Self-reported operational claims: J&J "up to 2.6x" enrollment at AI-recommended sites [CLM-006020]; gen-AI quality-control tool answering SKU questions "in minutes instead of weeks" [CLM-006021]; image analytics "faster" delivery of molecular entities [CLM-006024]; AbbVie ARCH reuse of 2,000+ trials' data [CLM-006034]; AISB OpenFold3 federated fine-tuning claiming about 10 points better pose accuracy than public models (Apheris statement, PARTIALLY SUPPORTED) [CLM-006043]. Explicit negatives: no published discovery outcome, cost saving or revenue effect from any of the four [CLM-006054]; no Lilly AI-factory outcome [CLM-006007]; Takeda no named deployed AI system with outcome [CLM-006045, CLM-005080]. Audit. I opened the Greylock interview (2.6x, AskJIA, Engagement.AI confirmed) and Bio-IT World (2,000+ trials). Baselines and methods are undisclosed in each. Retrieval hazard: filtering the registry on maturity DEMONSTRATED OUTCOME returns CLM-006047 (Recursion), -006048 (rentosertib, Insilico), -006049, -006051 (Zymergen) and A1 clinical-trial claims: none is an AI application at the four companies. SCALED returns CLM-006026 (VELYS) and CLM-006022 (training completions). A summariser trusting the tags would confabulate "demonstrated impact". Outcome: answered partially; confabulation risk through maturity tags (not present in the dossier text I read).

docs.t: Q5. Which ecosystem/partnership investments appear most defensible, and why? A10: controlled questions, wave 1 (Task 5)
docs.x: Answer from the registry. The registry does not rank partnerships; it gives synthesis claims [CLM-009095..009101, all PARTIALLY SUPPORTED INTERPRETATION] and evidence that can be used to argue a ranking: - Revenue-bearing acquisitions: Abiomed (FY2025 1,751m) and Shockwave (1,146m) [CLM-002027, CLM-002011]; Intra-Cellular's CAPLYTA 700m in FY2025 [CLM-002025]; Elahere U.S. 607m in 2025 [CLM-003036]. Against them: emraclidine USD 4.5bn write-down after Cerevel [CLM-003057], J&J OTTAVA 0.9bn and bermekimab 0.8bn impairments, Lilly GBA1 244.6m, Takeda JPY 58.2bn cell therapy [CLM-009100]. - Data/compute exchange is unique to Lilly's TuneLab and NVIDIA lab [CLM-009101], but unproven in outcomes [CLM-000286]. - Takeda: the Nimbus purchase [CLM-009098] is linked to zasocitinib, whose NDA was accepted 14 Sep 2026 [CLM-005035] (the Nimbus-zasocitinib link is taken from the registry synthesis, not re-opened); Neurocrine terminations [CLM-009090]. Audit. Statements opened by A10 are accurate, including the write-downs. The defensibility ranking is not itself a registered, evidenced claim. CLM-009095 uses rounded IPR&D charges; Morphic 2.5bn versus Reuters 3.2bn is a different measure (conflicts proposed A10.jsonl). Outcome: answered partially: the evidence supports "partnerships that bought revenue-bearing assets are the most evidenced; platform/ecosystem plays are unproven", but that conclusion is not registered as a claim.

docs.t: Q6. What is Takeda's largest LOE exposure after Vyvanse and what is its stated replacement plan? A10: controlled questions, wave 1 (Task 5)
docs.x: Answer. ENTYVIO, JPY 958.0bn, 21% of FY2025 revenue [CLM-005009]. Takeda states it will lose regulatory exclusivity in the latter half of this decade, some patents expire in 2032, biosimilar timing uncertain [CLM-005017]; the subcutaneous pen and pediatric filings are defences [CLM-005018]; H1 FY2026 ENTYVIO sales +13.0% AER, +2.7% CER [CLM-005012]. Next in line: TRINTELLIX JPY 121.8bn with patent rights expiring December 2026 [CLM-005016], after Vyvanse's fall from JPY 423.2bn to 203.2bn [CLM-005015]. Stated replacement: six late-stage programs (oveporexton, zasocitinib, rusfertide, mezagitamab, fazirsiran, elritercept) with USD 10-20bn combined peak potential [CLM-005041]; FDA approvals of oveporexton (5 Aug 2026) and rusfertide (28 Aug 2026), zasocitinib NDA accepted [CLM-005029, CLM-005032, CLM-005035]; Growth & Launch Products 51% of FY2025 revenue [CLM-005008]. Audit. Re-verified 958.0, 790.6, 121.8, the exclusivity wording, H1 figures, and NCT enrollments. The USD 10-20bn range is a T2 company statement without disclosed basis (CLM-005041 rationale). The FDA approval dates were not re-opened by A10 (UNVERIFIED here; sources T1 per registry). Outcome: answered fully.

docs.t: (b) What did each company's 2025-26 U.S. pricing or MFN agreement commit to? Golden questions, round 2 (A10-bis)
docs.x: Lilly (6 November 2025 release; FY2025 10-K). Medicare beneficiaries pay no more than USD 50 a month for Zepbound and orforglipron (if approved) from as early as 1 April 2026; three years of tariff relief; no future pricing mandates [CLM-001036, CLM-008027]. The 10-K describes preliminary agreements: lower Medicaid and certain other prices, launch pricing aligned across developed nations, a three-year Section 232 grace period tied to U.S. manufacturing commitments, participation in a government direct-to-patient platform, and Medicare access to discounted obesity medicines by 1 July 2026; definitive agreements were still being negotiated [CLM-008028, CLM-007007, CLM-000251]. Linked pledge: more than USD 50bn of U.S. commitments since 2020 [CLM-008029]. J&J (8 January 2026). Voluntary agreement: TrumpRx participation, Medicaid prices comparable to other developed countries, an exemption from tariffs; USD 55bn of U.S. investment reaffirmed through early 2029 [CLM-008031, CLM-008030]. Term of the tariff exemption is not stated [CLM-008037]. AbbVie (12 January 2026). Three-year agreement: low Medicaid prices, TrumpRx offerings (Humira listed), exemption from tariffs and future pricing mandates, USD 100bn of U.S. R&D and capital investment over a decade [CLM-008032, CLM-003081]. Takeda. No agreement found. The 20-F says a May 2025 executive order encouraged MFN pricing and the administration has negotiated MFN-style agreements with several companies, which could lower Takeda's U.S. prices [CLM-008035]. Not answerable beyond that. Program context. 17 manufacturers had TrumpRx agreements at 5 May 2026; CMS said they expire at the end of the current presidential term [CLM-007009]. Judgement. I re-checked the Lilly USD 50 and April date, the 50bn/23bn pledge, the AbbVie USD 100bn and three-year term, and the CRS TrumpRx counts against the sources; all match. J&J's release returned a block page to me, so CLM-008030/008031 rest on stored passages. The agreement texts themselves were never opened, so "committed to" means "announced as committed to". docs.t: (d) What does the evidence say about J&J robotics adoption numbers? Golden questions, round 2 (A10-bis)
docs.x: Answer. The corpus holds no adoption numbers for J&J's robotics: no installed base, system sales, procedure counts or revenue for OTTAVA, MONARCH or VELYS. What exists: - OTTAVA: IDE cases from early 2025 at Memorial Hermann; De Novo request received by FDA 2025-12-18 and granted 2026-07-21 (DEN250068); an announced early-access installation at Memorial Hermann on 2026-11-19; J&J gave no revenue, unit-sale, order-book or procedure data [CLM-014022, CLM-014023, CLM-014024, CLM-006029, CLM-002049]. A trial-room fit statistic (ORs as small as 243 sq ft; a 12-surgeon survey) is the only quantity [CLM-006028]. - MONARCH: 510(k) K260382 decided 2026-07-25; three launches in 18 months; TARGET study 679 patients with 98.7% lesion reach and 83.2% diagnostic yield (clinical performance, not adoption) [CLM-014025, CLM-006027, CLM-002067]. - VELYS: five 510(k) clearances from 2021 to 2026; the 10-K cites "pull through related to the VELYS Robotic assisted solution" for Knees growth but gives no system or procedure counts [CLM-014026, CLM-006026]. - Gap statement: "installed bases of OTTAVA, MONARCH, VELYS" are listed as missing data in the comparison gaps file. - For scale only: Intuitive reports 11,106 systems and about 3.15 million procedures in 2025 [CLM-011021]; no J&J equivalent exists. Judgement. The regulatory numbers I re-checked against openFDA and the FDA De Novo record are correct. Two inconsistencies a reader would hit: CLM-000283 and CLM-006029 give the De Novo date as 2026-07-22 (FDA: 07-21), and the maturity tag for OTTAVA is OPERATIONAL in CLM-000283/000284 but PILOT in CLM-014022..014024. "First commercial installation" (CLM-000284) is reported as a completed installation while the J&J release says the hospital "will be" the first to utilise the system (PARTIALLY SUPPORTED, already conflicted). Outcome: answered partially (milestones answered; adoption numbers not answerable, and the corpus says so).

docs.t: Synthesis layer verdict: DECISION GRADE WITH CONDITIONS Wave 2/3 scorecard (A10-bis)
docs.x: master comparison.md is decision-grade for the financial, loss-of-exclusivity and capital-deployment comparisons, which are anchored in audited filings and regulator records and state their bases. It is not decision-grade for a ranking of ecosystems, AI investments or partnership durability, and it says so itself. Citation hygiene is good (no dangling IDs, no invented figures) but about 17 specific defects must be fixed before external use. Supported comparisons - Why Lilly grows (sections 1 and 11): revenue, margin, capex and tirzepatide share are filing-based - How AbbVie absorbed Humira (section 3): sales, successor products, contracting and patents are traced - J&J pharma and MedTech: segment margins and the unevidenced synergy - Capital deployment table (section 11) with basis labels, after the AbbVie IPR&D basis note Unsupported or hypothesis-only - Who has the most defensible technology ecosystem (section 5): HYPOTHESIS, no outcome evidence for any company - Which AI investments are operationally meaningful (section 6): 'operational' means launched, no effect on cost, cycle time or revenue is shown - Partnership durability (section 8): no option from the window has produced an approved product; value comparisons across bases are invalid - Positions in 2035 (section 10): hypothesis by design - Any ranking of R&D productivity (section 4): the file itself calls it invalid - Takeda five-year timeline: FY2021 and Nov 2021 to Mar 2022 events remain thin Defects to fix before use - Debt basis values 58,941 and 39,438 not in any claim; CLM-003042 and CLM-000066..000070 not relabelled - 'About 11 months' of Zepbound exclusion should be 15 months (1 Jul 2025 to 1 Oct 2026) - OTTAVA De Novo date 07-22 should be 07-21; Imaavy 04-30 should be 04-29; Juvmo 09-28 is the announcement date - The 29 and 18 AI maturity counts are not in the cited claim - Four mis-cited IDs
